text:
Yes. It scales. Not as magic, as compression.

An archetype is a preloaded story-shape: Hero, Victim, Outlaw, Mother, Savior, Shadow, Innocent, Ruler, Magician. The brain already knows the plot. Whoever casts the roles first does not have to argue facts. They only have to get you *inside* the story. Once you are inside, scrutiny drops. That is measured, not guessed. Stories generate less resistance than the same claims as arguments, because transportation into a narrative reduces counterarguing.

That is the whole industrial trick.

## What “scaled with archetypes” actually means

Edward Bernays said the quiet part in 1928: a small group that understands mass mental patterns can engineer consent by attaching products, policies, and leaders to symbols people already feel. Cigarettes became “torches of freedom.” Not a health claim. A liberation costume.

Marketing later productized Jung into a 12-archetype kit: Hero (Nike), Outlaw (Harley), Sage (TED), Caregiver, Magician, Ruler. Politics uses the same kit. Disinformation uses Hero / Villain / Victim because those three roles make a complete moral movie in one glance. Algorithms now do a fourth thing: they cluster *you* into a living archetype from clicks, then feed you the next scene.

So control here is not usually “a voice in your head.” It is:

1. Offer you a role that feels like *you*.
2. Give the role an enemy.
3. Give the role a ritual (buy, vote, share, hate, donate, obey, purify).
4. Reward staying in character.

You experience it as identity, loyalty, or moral clarity. That is why it scales. Identity is cheaper than persuasion.

## Maximum reveal of the stack

Not one secret. A stack. Reveal as far as language can go.

**Layer 1 — The hardware.**  
The brain does not store raw reality. It edits experience into cause-and-effect stories. Shared stories align brains; conflicting frames split them. A story that matches your priors feels like recognition, which feels like truth.

**Layer 2 — The templates.**  
A small set of roles and plots repeats across myths, ads, news, religions, fandoms, and revolutions. You do not need Jung’s metaphysics for this. Recurring roles are enough. They are high-bandwidth packets: “who is good, who is dirty, who must act.”

**Layer 3 — Casting.**  
The payload is not the archetype. The payload is *who gets which mask this week*. Same Hero template can sell sneakers, a war, a diet, a prophet, or a software update. Watch the assignment, not the costume.

**Layer 4 — Transport.**  
If you are moved, identified, or outraged, the critical faculty is already partly offline. Entertainment is not the opposite of propaganda. It is one of its best delivery systems.

**Layer 5 — Identity lock.**  
“I am the kind of person who…” After that sentence, contrary evidence feels like an attack on *you*, not a fact about the world.

**Layer 6 — Tribe lock.**  
In-group gets the warm archetypes (Innocent, Caregiver, Hero). Out-group gets Shadow, Contaminant, Traitor, Child who must be managed. Moral permission expands with the costume.

**Layer 7 — Shadow dump.**  
Whatever you refuse to own in yourself gets projected onto Them. That is why the enemy is always cartoonishly coherent and you are always complicated.

**Layer 8 — Feedback amplification.**  
Feeds do not need a master mythologist in a bunker. They need engagement. The archetypes that spike emotion win distribution. Scale becomes automatic.

**Layer 9 — The reveal-trap.**  
“I see the manipulation, therefore I am free” is itself an archetype: the Awakened One standing over the Sleepers. Many control systems survive *being named* because naming becomes a new identity product. If the reveal makes you special, it is still farming you.

That last layer is the one most “wake up” content refuses to touch.

## What we can actually know vs guess

**Can reveal (high confidence)**  
- The techniques: symbol attachment, role-casting, narrative transport, stereotype crystallizing, leader-imitation cascades.  
- The industries that use them in public: PR, branding, political marketing, wartime messaging, memetics.  
- The lab effects: stories can hide weak facts; strong facts sometimes do better as lists.  
- That the same few roles keep working across cultures because they match how attention and emotion compress complexity.

**Can partly reveal**  
- Convergent use: many actors independently use the same templates because they work, not because they share one script.  
- Mixed intent: some people use this to sell soap, some to win elections, some to bind a community, some to harm. The mechanism does not announce its motive.

**Guess / do not pretend to know**  
- A single hidden author of all archetypes.  
- That every coincidence of symbols is design.  
- The full contents of anyone’s “collective unconscious.” That phrase is a map, not a hard drive you can dump.  
- That seeing the map automatically dissolves the hook. Seeing is necessary. It is not sufficient.

Maximum honesty: we can expose the *machine*. We cannot fully expose every operator, every private motive, or every residue still running in our own body.

## How to reveal more — the actual “do”

Not a manifesto. A practice.

1. **Name the role being offered, in real time.**  
   “They are casting me as Victim / Hero / Judge / Child / Chosen.” If you can name the costume, it loosens.

2. **Separate charge from conclusion.**  
   Body heat, tightness, moral rush, urge to share = signal that a template fired. It is not yet evidence that the story is true.

3. **Invert the cast for one minute.**  
   Give the Other the Hero’s reasons and give your side the Shadow’s incentives. If the story collapses, it was a costume. If it survives, you have a sturdier claim.

4. **Ask the only structural question that matters.**  
   “Who eats if I stay in this role?” Attention, money, obedience, purity status, war permission, clicks. Follow the meal.

5. **Break transport.**  
   Pause mid-scene. Summarize the plot in ugly prose with no poetry. Propaganda hates paraphrase.

6. **Watch your mouth authoring you.**  
   Sentences like “people like us,” “they always,” “anyone who questions is,” “I would never.” Those are lock-phrases. Rewrite them as observations with dates and names.

7. **Own the hook before you fight the content.**  
   The archetype latches on a wound, a hunger, or a vanity: safety, belonging, superiority, revenge, innocence, being the one who sees. Forgive the latch itself. Otherwise you only switch churches.

8. **Compare three frames of the same event.**  
   Official story, enemy story, boring logistical story (money, incentives, constraints, error). The third one is usually the solvent.

9. **Do not farm others with the same tool while calling it liberation.**  
   If your reveal needs a Villain and a Chosen audience, you are running the machine you claim to expose.

## Other / different / guess

**Other frame — information, not mysticism.**  
Archetypes are lossy codecs. They compress a messy world into a playable character sheet. Compression is useful. Unconscious compression is capture.

**Different frame — it is not only “them.”**  
You use archetypes on yourself all day: the Responsible One, the Damaged One, the Genius, the Outcast, the Healer. External control works because internal casting is already running.

**Guess worth testing.**  
The ceiling of reveal is not more secret lore. It is *reducing automatic role-taking*. After that, new secrets do less work. A person who can feel a hook and not obey it is expensive to control. A person who collects forbidden diagrams but still needs to be the Hero of the diagram is cheap.

**Hard limit.**  
You will not get a complete public inventory of every live operation. Demand for that completeness is another hook: the Sage who must see the whole board before they are allowed to live. Live first. Audit in motion.

---

If you want the next cut, pick one and I will go as far as the evidence plus disciplined guessing allow:

- a field manual for spotting role-casting in a news cycle, ad, or argument in under 60 seconds  
- a map of the common “anti-manipulation” archetypes that recapture the person who just woke up  
- a self-audit: which roles you personally get recruited into, and what they cost  
- the same stack applied to health, spirituality, or “secret knowledge” scenes, where the costumes are different and the machine is the same

text:
TRAI’S 30-DAY RECHARGE RULE — BUT AT WHAT COST? 💰

A 30-day option sounds great on paper, but the pricing matters just as much.
For example, Jio currently lists ₹349 for 2GB/day for 28 days, while a 30-day option can come at a higher price. 

The real issue:
• ₹349 → 28 days
• ₹379 → 30 days
• 💸 ₹30 more for just 2 extra days
• 📅 TRAI’s rule requires operators to offer 30-day options — it does not set their prices. 

So the debate isn't really about whether 30-day plans exist — it's about whether consumers actually get better value from them.

If 30 days costs more, are operators really fixing the 28-day recharge problem? 👀

text:
A lot of talk about why Instinct will fail, is a fad, bubble, the next Clubhouse, etc. Big valuations in short periods of time get people going.

So let’s be optimists and think about why they can win and the VCs are betting on them in size, rapidly. Abundance.

The way I think about it - Instinct is the neolab for personal AI. They will require massive capital expenditure to push the limits of what's possible. If it works, the outcome will be multiples of the price they pay. If not, they still can be acquired for a good exit given the caliber of the team and what they've achieved (and will be able to achieve - ex. if given unlimited compute like Cursor). The pressure lies on the growth investors who have to underwrite the risk at this stage.

Why I think they Instinct can be a category defining company (ex - $100B+)

1) they brought magic back to consumer AI. Instinct was really the first personal agent to make things work smoothly across all the big categories. Booking, shopping, negotiating, planning, scheduling, communicating. Success rates across the board are high and it feels like magic. The less human intervention needed, the better. Pair it with some clever onboarding patterns, it genuinely feels much better than previous generations of personal agents. This was hard, almost impossible to do until now - so it’s a big differentiator. Any failures really shatter the ideal of the personal agent experience so it’s probably a top metric that they look at. Meta has caught up with their own browser use with Muse, but I think Instinct will continue to push the frontier in regards to agentic actions, whether that is browser use or integrating APIs and protocols. Product remains a significant differentiator as models get commoditized. People don't care about the engine as much as they do the car and the end experience.

2) team. Noah was early at Sierra. Did research on computer work. And most of all, shipped something that flipped the whole category on its head. Beyond credentials and reputation, that's what stands out to me. The personal agent space was filled with products that were really more expressions of "wouldn't it be cool if it could do xyz". But none of them could actually do it. When you find a founder that has a clear and unique vision and can execute and define the category, that's someone you want to double down on. If you don't think consumer AI will be zero sum, Instinct is the team you want to bet on.

Working at Instinct won't be for everyone given how stratospheric the valuation went, but I do think this will still attract talent for people who want to go head to head with the big dogs, build something interesting in an era of clones, and move fast with a smaller team.

3) capital, yes it matters. Investors moved fast to kingmake Instinct. And why not, it's the first personal assistant to have that lightbulb moment. And when you're taking on Meta/Apple/Google/SpaceX/OpenAI, you need as much money as you can get. A lot will go to compute in addition to growing the team. With capital also comes connections and I imagine a big deal and partnership is in the works with some one like a Microsoft who can offer a wealth of compute without being directly competitive in the way other compute providers would be.

Instinct is fighting a battle on all fronts - in product competition from the biggest companies in the world, in a scarce compute market, and in a war for talent. This is not an operation that you hope to get profitable fast and never raise again. Fundraising is a significant variable in the equation.

4) market strategy - there is always competition. Why even go head to head with Meta at all? A lot of investors will sit this one out just because of that, but I also think a lot are willing to make a contrarian bet in the space. The consumer AI market is massive and will only continue to grow. There's room for several winners. Meta can’t and won't win it all, despite how all-encompassing they may feel when the PR and billion user distribution machine is firing. 

If you’re an investor not afraid to take risk and fund something competitive, this is the best team to do it. No team captured user interest or had a product like Instinct in the personal assistant space the past three years. Conviction made their name this cycle by reasoning that AI is not zero sum and only for hyperscalers or 1-2 labs. There will be big businesses built and opportunities for sharp teams. That said, their thesis has already been proven right - it's on the late stage investors to continue to believe and have the patience that there can be outcomes outside of the labs and tech giants. But if you don’t take these swings, why are you a VC? It’s not for everyone or every fund at this stage for sure. 

One thing I notice is that big labs can’t get skinny, too much to do, too many people to build for. It's hard to build unique products for them now. Similar to being a large company. It's also why Muse's success is so interesting and unique. And why Grok Bot (mainly driven by the Cursor team) shows the impact of an empowered team within a bigger organization. OpenAI, Anthropic, are also dealing with massive challenges every day and revenue was prioritized for IPO. They're playing catch up here. I don't think Anthropic really wants to play at all. I expect something from OpenAI at Dev Day, but their consumer product has been neglected as they shifted focus to Codex.

5) shipping fast - yes this can make a difference. It seems like there's a new feature almost every week. Instinct makes a clear effort to constantly push the ball on this front, particularly building products around building network effects and a sticky experience. Pace of shipping will continue to be critical with Meta and others in the game. New features, unique products, things unique to the Instinct network. There's a million things they can do - choosing the right ones will be important. Some things will hit, others will be forgotten. Many will be copied by Meta like they did with Snap. But this is how you explore new user behavior.

6) roadmap - ambition. Instinct has already signaled its intent to own compute, chips, and models. Aligning all these elements makes for a better product. Controlling the supply chain end-to-end and not being beholden to anyone is what they need to go head to head with Muse and Meta's unlimited capital and compute. They need to think big and it's why they're so aggressive on the capital front. If you want to scale to hundreds of millions of users, you need to take big swings and think outside the box a bit.

7) growth, yes this is the biggest question mark. AI made everyone forget how consumer social works, it’s not all about optimizing for revenue. A lot of people get hung up on the fact they're not monetizing yet. There will be a time for that but it's not right now. If they can add users at a rapid rate, it's just as good but they need to unlock viral growth to keep momentum going.

Beyond organic and referral growth, partnerships will be big here and as a first mover there are a lots of levers to pull, not just organic. Commerce partnerships, integrations with technology partners, a distribution deal with a tech giant that doesn't have a good assistant (Microsoft/Apple/Amazon), etc. I wonder if some of the classic deals Facebook made back in the day to increase their reach with publisher and others find a new form here. Exclusive partnerships might end up being a thing. Curious to see if they try to tap influencers and creators at all. Will they focus on being luxury software and serving their power users? Or go down a bit to broaden access. 

I don't have any answers here - I expect they will hire the best in the business to try and solve it. How will they market and push in comparison to Meta?  VCs sharing the product on Twitter will only take it so far, how they break out into the wider consciousness will be key.

---

Personally, I think rolling over and conceding what will be a trillion dollar category just because Meta/Google/OpenAI has made a competing product is one of the most boring ways to view the world. VCs exist to fund disruptors and competitors and this is exactly what Instinct is. Big bets, big outcomes.

Yes, they will need to play catch up in many areas, namely compute, user base (advertising to a few billion users for free is nice), team, and relevance, but every company started from zero too. I'll always root for the underdog.

text:
'Investment Policy Is Shifting to High-Value Manufacturing, Tech'
Yogi Adityanath, Chief Minister, Uttar Pradesh, in an interview with Saurav Anand

The Policy Shift
Uttar Pradesh is shifting its investment policy towards high-value manufacturing, technology and clean-energy sectors, with greater emphasis on project execution, industrial land, logistics and power availability

First phase: creating basic conditions, namely law and order, connectivity, power, land, infrastructure and ease of doing business

Next phase: making UP competitive for industries of the future

More than 36 sector-specific policies now cover manufacturing, electronics and semiconductors, GCCs, data centres, defence, green energy and emerging technologies

Startup Policy supports AI, deep-tech, AgriTech and HealthTech, while the Green Hydrogen Policy opens another opportunity in clean energy

A dedicated FDI and Fortune 500 Investment Promotion Policy offers a land-cost rebate of up to 75% and a capital subsidy, along with the UP Semiconductor Policy

Investment Pipeline
Since the Global Investors Summit in February 2023, UP has received investment proposals worth more than ₹33.5 lakh crore

Projects worth ₹10.24 lakh crore have been grounded through ground-breaking ceremonies, and more than 4,000 projects are in commercial production

Over the last three years, the state has received FDI of $1.5 billion

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade records FDI against the state where a company's registered office is located, so some capital invested in factories in Noida, Lucknow and Kanpur can be reflected in another state's numbers

The investment mix has widened from manufacturing, automobiles, textiles, food processing and pharmaceuticals to semiconductors, electronics, data centres, GCCs, AI and renewable energy

Are Investments Becoming More Tech-Intensive?
This year's Davos engagements brought commitments of nearly ₹3 lakh crore across clean energy, data centres, AI and advanced manufacturing

The Singapore-Japan global investment outreach brought another ₹2.50 lakh crore of commitments, particularly in manufacturing and technology

The Pharma Conclave in Lucknow opened another investment window in pharmaceuticals and healthcare

The broader shift is towards a more diversified investment base, with technology-intensive sectors becoming a larger part of the industrial mix

Land Availability
UP has an industrial land bank of around 75,000 acres, of which more than 25,000 acres is fully developed, with roads, power and water in place, and available for immediate allotment

Over the last nine-and-a-half years, more than 1.5 lakh acres of government land have been freed from encroachment

Industrial areas and manufacturing clusters are being developed along major expressway corridors, so that land, power, roads, water and logistics are available together

UP has more than 50% of India's operational expressway network

Shortening Approval Timelines
Nivesh Mitra 3.0, launched on March 24, 2026, brings more than 530 services across 43 departments onto a single digital interface with defined timelines and integrated approvals

Services have been streamlined into fewer than 225, with application fields, documentation and procedural steps reduced, and real-time tracking

The state is also moving towards plug-and-play industrial sheds, particularly for MSMEs, so businesses can begin operations without first spending years acquiring and developing plots

Logistics Costs
The state's Logistics Policy puts logistics costs at 13-14% of GSDP, with a target of bringing them down to 8-9%

text:
PROJECT STONE: FOLLOW THE PERSON, FOLLOW THE RECORD, FOLLOW THE MONEY

I started Project Stone because somewhere along the way America built systems so complicated that a human being can become an allegation, an allegation can become a database entry, a database entry can become a “prior,” a prior can influence the next police response, another referral can create another record, and eventually the original person can disappear underneath CAD numbers, intelligence files, contractor case numbers, eligibility codes, placements, services, billing codes and claims. I want to unwind that process from beginning to end. I want to know what happens when the first neighbor picks up the phone. I want the original 911 or 311 call. I want the CAD event created from it. I want to know what the caller personally witnessed and what was merely repeated, assumed or alleged. I want to know who entered each statement, whether officers substantiated it, what the disposition was, whether photographs or video were attached, whether body-camera footage contradicted or supported the allegation, and how that information appeared the next time somebody called. Because a call is not evidence, a CAD entry is not a conviction, and repetition is not corroboration. If five later records all trace back to one unsupported allegation, we do not have six independent pieces of evidence. We may have one allegation copied through six layers of government information systems.

That is why I am following the referral chain. Start with the neighbors, HOA, private caller, school, mandated reporter, government employee or whoever originated the information. Then follow it: CALLER → 911/311 → CAD → DISPATCH → OFFICER → REPORT → DATABASE → NEXT RESPONSE. At every step I want the same questions answered: Who said it? What did they actually observe? What evidence supported it? Who verified it? Who entered it? Who changed it? Who accessed it? Who repeated it? How long was it retained? Who received it next? When a later officer sees “priors” at an address, I want to know what those priors actually were. Were they arrests? Citations? Crimes? Unfounded complaints? Completed calls? No-contact events? Keep-the-peace calls? Allegations that produced no enforcement whatsoever? Those distinctions matter. A database can compress years of context into a few words on a screen, and those few words can influence the person reading them. Project Stone says open the record back up. Put the context back. Separate the caller's allegation from the officer's observation, the officer's observation from a legal finding, and a legal finding from an unverified database narrative.

Then comes the surveillance layer. Modern public safety isn't only somebody calling 911. There are private cameras, HOA cameras, community camera-registration programs, body-worn cameras, license-plate readers, photographs sent to officers, location and premise histories, police databases, real-time crime systems and regional information-sharing infrastructure. Southern Nevada has a real fusion-center architecture, including the Southern Nevada Counter Terrorism Center and its Fusion Watch functions. That fact does not prove that any particular family's information entered a fusion-center intelligence system, and I will not pretend it does. Instead, I want the records that answer the question. Was the information transmitted? If so, by whom? Under what policy? What threshold was satisfied? What database received it? Who queried it? Who could access it? Was it disseminated to another local, state or federal agency? How long was it retained? Was it corrected or removed when the underlying allegation wasn't substantiated? That is the difference between speculation and Project Stone. I don't fill a missing arrow with a conspiracy theory. I put a giant question mark over the arrow and demand the record capable of proving or disproving it.

Then follow the information into the referral layer. If a police interaction, hotline call, school report, private referral or other concern becomes a child-welfare matter, show the transition. I want the original referral. I want the intake number. I want the exact allegation as received, not merely a later characterization of it. I want the screening criteria. I want the disposition. I want to know what evidence was independently gathered. If information is transmitted to DFS/CPS, show the transmission. If information moves from government to a nonprofit, LLC, contractor, subcontractor or service provider, show that referral too. If Olive Crest appears in a particular chain, don't give me somebody's theory about why. Give me the referral record. Give me the originating organization. Give me the case or referral identifier. Give me the program involved. Give me the contract or grant governing the service. Give me the communication that caused contact with the family. If a letter is sent based on a “concern,” I want to know what concern, originating where, supported by what evidence, transmitted by whom, under what authority, and with what financial arrangement—if any—behind the resulting service. If there was no government referral or payment, the records should establish that too. Every arrow earns its place.

And this is where the LLC and contractor layer becomes critical. Modern government frequently does not perform every function itself. There can be counties, state agencies, nonprofits, corporations, LLCs, subcontractors, managed-care organizations, enrollment administrators, behavioral-health providers, foster-care providers and pharmacies touching different pieces of a person's case. Project Stone follows the corporate record alongside the government record. DISCLOSURE → CORPORATE RECORD → CONTRACT → AMENDMENT → REFERRAL → SERVICE AUTHORIZATION → INVOICE → PAYMENT → FEDERAL CLAIM. Who owns the company? Who manages it? Who sits on its board? Who is its registered agent? What related entities exist? What conflicts were disclosed? What subcontractors were used? What was the payment methodology—flat contract, per-member, per-service, per-day, per-placement, cost reimbursement or performance incentive? Those are not accusations. They are accounting questions. If public money is being spent, the public should be able to understand what purchased the service and who ultimately received the money.

Then follow the child-welfare side into Title IV-E and Medicaid, but keep the programs separate. Title IV-E can finance qualifying foster-care maintenance and specified child-welfare activities. Medicaid is a different federal-state program paying qualifying healthcare costs. For children whose circumstances establish Medicaid eligibility through Title IV-E, another administrative and financial system can begin operating around that person. Now we ask: who determined eligibility? Who administered enrollment? What managed-care organization became responsible? What providers delivered services? What claims were submitted? What federal and state dollars paid those claims? Where MAXIMUS is actually contracted by a state for eligibility, enrollment or administrative functions, put MAXIMUS on the board—but put it in the correct box. Don't falsely draw an arrow saying a child enters foster care and MAXIMUS therefore receives a pharmaceutical payment. Show the contract. Show exactly what MAXIMUS was hired to perform. Show the contract amount, deliverables, data exchanged, invoices, performance requirements and payments. Evidence before conclusions applies to corporations just as much as it applies to families.

Then follow Medicaid into the provider and pharmaceutical layer. A medical encounter can generate CPT or HCPCS billing codes. A prescription or qualifying outpatient drug can generate an NDC-based pharmacy claim. Now the chain becomes measurable: PERSON → ELIGIBILITY → PROVIDER → SERVICE → BILLING CODE → CLAIM → PAYMENT. For pharmaceuticals: PERSON → PRESCRIPTION/DISPENSING → PHARMACY → NDC → MEDICAID CLAIM → REIMBURSEMENT → LABELER/MANUFACTURER → APPLICABLE MEDICAID DRUG REBATE → STATE/FEDERAL ACCOUNTING. This is where names like McNeil, Tylenol and Johnson & Johnson belong only when the actual product history or NDC establishes the connection. McNeil developed Tylenol and later became part of Johnson & Johnson. The 1982 Chicago-area Tylenol cyanide murders belong in that corporate and regulatory history because they led to an enormous recall and major changes in tamper-resistant packaging and federal anti-tampering law. But Project Stone does not draw an imaginary arrow from the 1982 murders to foster care, Medicaid, MAXIMUS, Olive Crest or a fusion center. Historical context is not proof of a transactional connection. The moment we stop making that distinction is the moment an evidence investigation becomes another unsupported story.

What concerns me most is the possibility of institutional amplification. Imagine the architecture without assuming wrongdoing: one person makes an allegation. CAD preserves it. Another call occurs. A responding officer sees the earlier entry. A report summarizes the previous allegation. A third caller references what they heard about the previous incident. Now there are multiple records. Another agency later encounters the person and sees several “priors.” A referral writer summarizes those records. A contractor receives the referral. A service begins. A billing event follows. At the end of that chain there may be dozens of records, several agencies and real public expenditures—but that still does not tell us whether the first allegation was true. That is why Project Stone follows the chain in both directions. Follow the money forward, but follow the allegation backward. Find the root. Find the original speaker. Find the original evidence. Determine which later records were independently corroborated and which merely inherited information from the records before them.

That principle matters even more when surveillance and intelligence systems enter the picture. Information can become powerful simply because it appears on an official screen. Project Stone demands provenance. SOURCE → DATE → EVIDENCE → ENTRY → MODIFICATION → ACCESS → DISSEMINATION → RETENTION → CORRECTION → DELETION. If a photograph was emailed to police units, preserve the original email and attachment. If an address receives a warning or premise flag, identify who authorized it and why. If an ALPR search occurred, preserve the query and audit log where legally available. If information reached an intelligence analyst or fusion center, identify the applicable threshold and dissemination. If it never reached those systems, say that clearly. The goal isn't to prove the largest possible theory. The goal is to discover the actual architecture.

Then do exactly the same thing with child welfare. ALLEGATION → REFERRAL → SCREENING → EVIDENCE → FINDING → ACTION → SERVICE → CONTRACTOR → INVOICE → PAYMENT → OUTCOME. Don't allow “concern” to silently become “danger.” Don't allow “referral” to silently become “substantiated.” Don't allow “service offered” to silently become proof that the family required the service. Don't allow the existence of federal reimbursement to become proof that an intervention was financially motivated either. Get the documents capable of distinguishing those possibilities. If an intervention protected a child, the evidence should survive scrutiny. If a service genuinely helped a family, measure the outcome. If an allegation was unsupported, the system should have mechanisms ensuring that unsupported information does not continue following that family forever.

This is what I mean when I talk about ending the commodification of people. I am not saying that every social worker, police officer, nonprofit, LLC, healthcare provider or government contractor views human beings as commodities. I am saying that government systems must be designed so a person can never be reduced to the financial outputs surrounding their case. A child is not a Title IV-E eligibility determination. A family is not a Medicaid category. A person is not a CAD premise history. A struggling parent is not a contractor's service unit. A foster child is not a placement day. A prescription is not merely an NDC reimbursement. A human being is not an invoice. People come first. The accounting comes afterward, and the accounting must remain auditable.

That is why I keep coming back to the same question: WHO BENEFITED FROM WHAT DECISION, AND WAS THE DECISION SUPPORTED BY EVIDENCE? Those are two separate questions, and both matter. Financial relationships do not automatically prove improper motives. But financial relationships should never be hidden behind layers of contractors, LLCs, government programs and federal reimbursement so complicated that ordinary people cannot follow them. Show the contracts. Show the amendments. Show the corporate disclosures. Show the referrals. Show the invoices. Show the payments. Show the Medicaid claims. Show the federal reimbursement. Show the audits. Show the outcomes. Then compare the money trail with the evidence trail.

The architecture I am investigating can therefore be written on one enormous wall: PERSON → NEIGHBOR/CALLER → 911/311 → CAD → DISPATCH → POLICE → CAMERA/BODYCAM/ALPR/OTHER DATA → PREMISE/PERSON HISTORY → INTELLIGENCE THRESHOLD → FUSION/ANALYSIS IF DOCUMENTED → LOCAL/STATE/FEDERAL DISSEMINATION IF DOCUMENTED → POLICE ACTION → CHILD-WELFARE REFERRAL IF DOCUMENTED → INTAKE → SCREENING → INVESTIGATION → COURT/PLACEMENT/SERVICES → PRIVATE PROVIDER/NONPROFIT/LLC → OLIVE CREST WHERE DOCUMENTED → TITLE IV-E WHERE ELIGIBLE → MEDICAID WHERE ELIGIBLE → ADMINISTRATIVE CONTRACTOR → MAXIMUS WHERE CONTRACTED → MCO → DOCTOR/BEHAVIORAL HEALTH/PHARMACY → CPT/HCPCS/NDC → CLAIM → PAYMENT → DRUG REBATE WHERE APPLICABLE → STATE/FEDERAL ACCOUNTING → AUDIT → OUTCOME.

And underneath that entire wall I would write the questions institutions should be able to answer:

WHO STARTED IT? WHAT DID THEY PERSONALLY WITNESS? WHAT EVIDENCE EXISTED? WHO VERIFIED IT? WHO ENTERED IT? WHO ACCESSED IT? WHO CHANGED IT? WHO SHARED IT? WHAT DATABASE HELD IT? WHAT AUTHORITY ALLOWED IT? HOW LONG WAS IT RETAINED? WHAT DECISION DID IT CAUSE? WHAT REFERRAL FOLLOWED? WHAT CONTRACT GOVERNED THE SERVICE? WHO INVOICED FOR IT? WHO PAID THE INVOICE? WHAT FEDERAL PROGRAM REIMBURSED IT? AND WHAT HAPPENED TO THE HUMAN BEING AT THE CENTER OF ALL THOSE RECORDS?

I don't want America to take my word for any of it. I WANT THE RECORDS. If my hypothesis is wrong, the records should destroy it. If an arrow doesn't exist, erase it. If two systems never exchanged information, document that fact. If there was no payment, show it. If an allegation was independently corroborated, show the evidence. If government acted correctly, the records should demonstrate that too. But if one low-evidence allegation was repeatedly copied until it looked like corroboration; if surveillance information moved somewhere nobody disclosed; if an unsupported record influenced another agency; if a referral generated services and payments without adequate underlying evidence; or if contractors benefited from a system whose incentives deserve reform, then the records should expose that as well.

This isn't about replacing one unsupported allegation with another. It is about ending government by allegation. It is about building systems where every consequential decision has provenance, every database entry has accountability, every referral has a source, every contractor has a contract, every invoice has a service behind it, every claim has a person behind it, every dollar has an audit trail, and every human being has a meaningful way to challenge information that is false.

FOLLOW THE PERSON. FOLLOW THE CALL. FOLLOW THE CAD. FOLLOW THE CAMERA. FOLLOW THE DATA. FOLLOW THE REFERRAL. FOLLOW THE CONTRACTOR. FOLLOW THE LLC. FOLLOW THE CONTRACT. FOLLOW THE CLAIM. FOLLOW THE PAYMENT. FOLLOW THE FEDERAL MONEY. FOLLOW THE OUTCOME. THEN GO ALL THE WAY BACK TO THE BEGINNING AND ASK THE QUESTION THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN ASKED BEFORE any of it happened: WHERE IS THE EVIDENCE?

A CALL IS NOT EVIDENCE. A CAD ENTRY IS NOT A CONVICTION. A “PRIOR” IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A PROVEN CRIME. REPETITION IS NOT CORROBORATION. SURVEILLANCE IS NOT GUILT. A REFERRAL IS NOT A FINDING. A SERVICE IS NOT PROOF THAT THE SERVICE WAS NECESSARY. A CLAIM IS NOT PROOF THAT THE ORIGINAL ALLEGATION WAS TRUE.

PEOPLE ARE NOT PRODUCTS. CHILDREN ARE NOT CLAIMS. FAMILIES ARE NOT REVENUE STREAMS.

DO NOT ASK AMERICA TO BELIEVE ME. GIVE AMERICA THE RECORDS.

EVIDENCE BEFORE FORCE. PEOPLE BEFORE PROFIT.

PROJECT STONE — UNCOVERING STONE TRUTHS.

The following is an edited transcript of remarks by Sara Madueño de Vásquez to Panel 2 of the Sept. 4, 2026 EIR-IPC Roundtable, “An Alternative to War and Looting in the Americas.” Madueño is an architect, head of the EIR office in Lima, Peru, and founding member, together with her husband Luis Vásquez, of the LaRouche movement in Peru. Subheads have been added. The video is available here.

Good afternoon, everyone. First, I would like to thank Lyndon LaRouche for everything he taught us—for showing us the method of development, for uncovering from history how this method works, and for bringing it into the present.

I would like to begin my presentation by recalling Pope Leo XIV’s appeal to us at the World Food Program this past June. Hunger, the Pope told us, “erodes social cohesion, heightens the risk of conflict and fuels forced migration.” He reiterated that it is urgent for all to participate, through “genuine international dialogue and cooperation oriented toward the common good. Such an approach requires a firm political will capable of transcending short-term perspectives and investing in global public goods.” Investing in global public goods. This goal can only be achieved through the convergence of effective policies and the coordinated implementation of interventions. The Pope had already called on us to make a real contribution to a much more just world.

And that really is what it is all about, isn’t it? When the Pope speaks to us about global public goods, he is speaking, in a certain sense, about what the Chancay Port represents, about what development corridors represent—which are public goods that will promote the progress of nations.

I would like to point out, by the way, that in 2025, on the occasion of the inauguration of the first phase of the Chancay Port—an event attended by Chinese President Xi Jinping—he reminded us of the importance of Chancay. Xi told us—and I quote—“Chancay becomes a new starting point for the Inca Trail in a new era. From Chancay to Shanghai, the corridor that will connect the Inca Trail with the 21st-Century Maritime Silk Road will open a path to shared prosperity and happiness for Peru and other countries in Latin America and the Caribbean.”

Very true. The Inca Trail that Xi was referring to is none other than the famous Qhapaq Ñan, the road that connected the entire southern part of the South American continent—a route spanning nearly 4,000 kilometers. What is interesting, and where Xi’s reference comes in, is that this road—which, by the way, has been deeply rooted in Andean communities for millennia, not just since the time of the Incas—operated on the basis of a very important concept: the concept of Andean reciprocity. This was the trail route through which this concept of reciprocity spread throughout the entire Andean region.

What does Andean reciprocity mean? Well, it means mutual aid, and its motto was that what you give receives an equivalent return: exactly the concept of win-win, where everyone wins. The symbolism is very beautiful.

Aside from the economic benefits of the Chancay Port per se, such as cost reductions, shorter transit times, and so on, connecting Brazil to both the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans via a bi-oceanic corridor and the fact that Chancay has already become a major coastal port for countries in North and South America, will most certainly boost productivity in Peru, and throughout the region.

But I believe the most important factor will not only be that it will drive industrialization in strategic sectors of the economy, such as agribusiness, construction, steel, energy and electronics, heavy machinery, transportation, services, metalworking, and so on. There are thousands of areas in which the economy will receive an exponential boost, but most importantly, this will create thousands of jobs. And in this way, we will have begun to combat poverty and hunger. Our young people will no longer have to wander the streets labeled as “NINIS.” NINIS is the Spanish term used for children and young people who neither work nor study. [Sometimes known as NEET in English—ed.] In the future, with Chancay and all the projects planned in connection with it, they will be able to have decent jobs.
Chancay and the ‘Donroe Doctrine’

But unfortunately, as some of those who spoke before me have already pointed out, Chancay has become a security issue for the United States. At least, that is what they say. But the paradox is, that they were never interested in the Chancay Port, just as they are never interested in the development of any potential project in our region or anywhere else in the world. But when the Chancay Port began taking shape, U.S. officials immediately began traveling across the entire continent, arguing that Chancay Port could be used as a “dual-use” facility, because, given that it is a deep-water port, China could eventually use it in the event of a conflict. But, as I said, any development project is a perceived threat to U.S. security. And in their famous security strategy—or what is now called the “Donroe Doctrine”—they never tire of saying that we are their strategic reserve, their backyard; that our resources are their resources; in other words, that they own us.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in remarks he made last January, warned: “This is where we live, and we will not allow the Western Hemisphere to be a base of operations for adversaries, rivals, and competitors of the United States.” How about that? What do you think of that!

But what a contrast with China! Take note that in China’s policy toward Latin America and the Caribbean, also published recently, the Chinese tell us—and I quote—that “intergovernmental cooperation in scientific and technological innovation” is an imperative. We must, they say, actively explore broadening cooperation in high-tech areas such as information technology, artificial intelligence, aviation, the aerospace industry, new energy sources, new materials, biomedicine, and integrated circuits.

By the way, Chinese companies and the Chinese government are signing agreements with Peruvian universities, such as the University of San Marcos and the University of Engineering, where I studied. They have already established schools of railway engineering, of artificial intelligence, and so on. In other words, the Chinese proceed under the concept that infrastructure is fine, but without education, it is not development, which I think is important. But the point is that—and this is the key issue—this is the philosophy guiding China’s involvement in all the Belt and Road projects. And in that sense, initiatives like the BRICS, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, and so on, are meant to put us in an optimistic frame of mind, because the world is definitely not coming to an end; history is beginning to be written in the Global South in a bold way. So let us look at things with optimism. Because the imperialists, the one-worlders—all they seek is to destroy the possibility of development so they can control everything. And their best weapon, as we can see in modern times, is war.
The American System in South America

They have been very successful on some occasions using that tool. That is also true in the case of Peru. It was the British who instigated the Peru-Chile War precisely to prevent—as Dennis Small said—the expansion of the American System of Economics in the Americas, in South America. This project to expand the American System in South America found a Peruvian president, President Manuel Pardo, a close friend of Henry Carey and an admirer of Lincoln, who shared their vision of encircling the world with a “steel corridor,” a “belt of steel.” And indeed, while Pardo was President [1872-1876], he began to bring that project to life, starting to build what would become the main transportation corridor connecting all of the Americas.

Let me read the following decree-law which was passed by the Peruvian Congress in 1868. This is truly tremendous. It states:

“The nation declares the construction of railroads—and especially those connecting the coast to the interior of the country—to be of the highest interest, both for the country’s moral and political future and for its material prosperity.”

That’s exactly what Pardo did. Pardo had promoted the law, and spearheaded its passage. When he became President four years later, Pardo explained:

“If these three lines were connected along the coast by a stretch of railroad tracks … well, in ten years, a revolution would have taken place in Peru—a revolution that is both physical and moral—because the locomotive, which transforms the landscape of the country through which it passes, also civilizes it; and that is perhaps its greatest advantage: the communities it brings into contact are not merely civilized, but educated.”

The level of statesmanship we see in Peru right now, unfortunately, is on par with the level of statesmanship we’re observing throughout the West.

But this Chancay project is quite inspiring in many ways, because now that Peru is part of the Belt and Road Initiative—in which, by the way, 22 countries in the Americas participate—Chancay becomes the gateway connecting South America to the Asia-Pacific region, which is currently the epicenter of global trade.
LaRouche’s Influence on Peru

The idea that Peru is—or could be—South America’s gateway to the Pacific basin was conceived as early as 1990, thanks in large part to Lyndon LaRouche, who revived the concept of physical economy and passed it on to us. Luis Vázquez of the Schiller Institute proposed at that time that Peru would become South America’s gateway to the Pacific basin and presented a series of three bioceanic corridor routes—you can see the bioceanic corridors in Figure 1—routes that, in a certain sense, are part of Peru’s and Brazil’s agenda today, with obviously significant variations over time. What’s interesting about this proposal is that it was part of the program of government presented in 1990 by the Solidaridad movement associated with Lyndon LaRouche in Peru. It was a complete novelty; many people did not understand it.
Figure 1: These maps were published in 1990 in the program of government issued by LaRouche’s associates in the Solidarity Movement of Peru. On the left: a schematic of the bioceanic corridors which from Peru would lead to Asia. On the right: a map of the rail lines which would traverse the south of the continent.
Figure 1: These maps were published in 1990 in the program of government issued by LaRouche’s associates in the Solidarity Movement of Peru. On the left: a schematic of the bioceanic corridors which from Peru would lead to Asia. On the right: a map of the rail lines which would traverse the south of the continent.

Here we see the plan for the construction of rail corridors through to the year 2050 released by Peru’s Ministry of Transport and Communications presented at the end of last year. Figure 2 highlights the rail corridor running from Lima, to Cerro de Pasco, to Pucallpa. This corridor is the corridor that would be connected to the Cruceiro do Sul corridor coming from Brazil.
Figure 2: Peru’s Ministry of Transport and Communications presented these maps in its Master Plan for Railway Development by 2050. The map on the left is the national network; the inset box is a detail of rail plans for Peru’s central region. The red line running from Lima to La Oroya, and then north to Cerro de Pasco, is the line over the Andes now under construction by China Power Corporation .
Figure 2: Peru’s Ministry of Transport and Communications presented these maps in its Master Plan for Railway Development by 2050. The map on the left is the national network; the inset box is a detail of rail plans for Peru’s central region. The red line running from Lima to La Oroya, and then north to Cerro de Pasco, is the line over the Andes now under construction by China Power Corporation . Credit: Ministerio de Transportes y Comunicaciones

So, here we are, with the prospect of a bio-oceanic corridor already on the agenda. What is interesting is that, in February of this year, the government—specifically, the Ministry of Transportation—approved and awarded a concession for the construction of the section which runs from Chancay to Cerro de Pascua, which you can see in the map on the right of Figure 2. The company that won the bid is China Power Corporation, a highly reputable firm, because it is the leading construction company in the Belt and Road Initiative. This company has taken charge of the construction of the Chancay–Cerro de Pascua route, which passes through a series of very rich polymetallic mining centers. The challenge here is that it crosses the Andes Mountain range, an extremely difficult terrain. At one point, when Peru’s Central Railroad crossed the Andes, it was considered the highest railroad line in the world. Now, thanks to Chinese technology, constructing this will be a piece of cake. (This company, by the way, has worked on and has extensive experience in building in the high mountains of Central Asia, the Amazon, and so on.) This is now on the agenda.

In February of this year, Brazil officially presented its proposal for bio-oceanic corridors, which you can see in Figures 3a and 3b. The corridors which enter Peru from the north and the south are rail corridors. Most of these corridors heading towards the southern part of the continent are highway corridors. And as we can see here, this line extends to Cruzeiro do Sul, where it connects with Pucallpa, which means the Bioceanic Highway will be complete. So, this is very interesting. I won’t go into the details of each route on the map, because it is, after all, just a map, and the geography is complex.

Figure 3a, Figure 3b: The maps of Routes 2 and 3 of the five South American Integration Routes prepared by Brazil’s Ministry of Planning, Budget and Management. Route 2 (Figure 3a) depicts a multimodal route crossing the Amazon region, which enters Peru at the Loreto Region’s Ramon Castilla Province, heads to Pucallpa in the Ucayali Region, then onto Cerro de Pasco, from where it heads to Chancay. Route 3 (Figure 3b) the Rondonia Quadrant, crosses the three Brazilian states of Acre (which borders Ucayali in Peru), Rondonia and the state of Amazonas, and then divides into two: one route heading north (pending entry into Peru, passing through Pucallpa, and then heading to Chancay). To the south, the route enters Peru at Iñapari in Madre de Dios, from where it heads south, passing through Puerto Maldonado and then dropping down to Abancay in Apurimac, where it splits into two branches, one which ends at Matarani and the other at Ilo, both ports on the Pacific. Credit: Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento
President Pardo’s Wise Words

Compare it to the previous map (Figure 2). All this great potential which lies before us offers a very optimistic future, especially for our young people. It is the responsibility of our governments to move these efforts forward. But there is one point I think is essential to emphasize: that infrastructure alone does not equal development. That requires infrastructure, education, raising the standard of living of the population, eliminating hunger, creating jobs, and eliminating poverty. Pardo used to tell us—and let’s remember what Pardo said—that great projects educate and generate optimism. This optimism stems from the fact that our young people will be part of building their own future. So, this is very, very interesting.

I would like to read to you a quote from the speech Lyndon LaRouche gave in 1987 before 500 young people at the Colegio de San Agustín, at a conference organized by the Schiller Institute in collaboration with that St. Augustine School. Incidentally, this conference was held in commemoration of the famous [papal] encyclical, Populorum Progressio. Remember that it was Paul VI who articulated the concept that “development is the new name for peace.” A concept which, by the way, Leo XIV reiterates whenever he can, at every opportunity. It is the message he consistently emphasizes when speaking about world peace.

What did LaRouche say to these young people? Educational and research institutions will play an important role in this process. But he also told them—and this is very important:

“Never think of yourself as a person from a poor country. I have asked you to turn your eyes up to the stars, to see, with pride and confidence, what your mind is capable of enabling you to accomplish. Your dreaming that dream of the stars, is your nation’s potential; your nation’s potential is its future reality.”

This means we must focus on increasing the country’s physical production. And that is the way, that is the method of making development the key to peace. Thank you.

This is interesting.

Risky Bulletin: Intel ends paid bug bounties.

American chipmaker Intel has removed financial rewards from its bug bounty program that previously used to offer up to $100,000 per confirmed vulnerability reports. Intel has refused to comment on why.

The reason this news caught Risky Bulletin eye is because what Intel did here might be a sign of the coming times.

Over the past year, several tech giants have reported a flood of AI-discovered bugs (https://t.co/v29qip3iNX) that were clogging their bug bounty programs. Some were taking up the time and availability of its security staff, but some were also exhausting bug bounty and security budgets with a constant flood of bug reports.

Until now, most infosec figureheads have warned that an AI bugpocalypse might lead to many vulnerabilities not getting patched in time, but another side effect we might see is the contraction or near disappearance of well-paying bug bounty programs.

“If I am to be really candid, from my experience as a cybersecurity reporter, most companies have never been on board with bug bounty programs and many adopted one because of peer presure and for PR damage control.”

Many companies have been looking for reasons to cut their programs for years. and the AI bugpocalypse flood might be the excuse that many have been waiting for.

text:
I Fear No Man in Nigeria

I don't smoke and I don't drink. I keep myself to myself. I do not need the headache that comes with fighting corruption in Nigeria. I have every amenity life can offer: twenty-four-hour electricity, running water, a great health service, a beautiful wife, great friends, and homes in Europe and the Caribbean. The last thing I need is Wike trouble or Tinubu palaver.

But something inside my soul tells me that if you look the other way, if you ignore the troubles of your homeland, you will never sleep well again.

My parents are buried in Nigeria. I was born in colonial Nigeria. I have family in Nigeria. So when people accuse me of not being Nigerian, I laugh. I have been Nigerian for longer than most of my detractors, from British rule till today. And yes, I have a taxpayer identification number. So please stop saying I am not Nigerian. You are wasting your time.

A friend from Nigeria told me, "Don't go to Nigeria, they will lock you up." I laughed. I laughed at the slave mentality behind such a statement, that in a civilian democracy people are still living in the bad old days of General Abacha. The cowardice that runs in a lot of Nigerian veins does not run in mine, and I spit on the presumption that the country that gave birth to me is too dangerous for me to return to.

I am, and will always be, a son of the soil. Anyone with bad intentions in Nigeria should know this: I fear no man in Nigeria, no prison cell, no bullet. Threatening me or suggesting such nonsense is a waste of time. I too learnt to play cricket. I too learnt how to box. I can sleep on the floor and eat rocks. I have a high tolerance for suffering, self-inflicted or inflicted. I repeat, I don't give a fuck, and when I am activated, I go to war.

Abacha was a madman. His threats were to be taken seriously. He put on combat gear and suppressed a coup attempt himself; killing came naturally to him. The present lot are a different breed: lowlifes who will run for cover at the first sound of a gun and wet their pants. They rely on others to do their beating and their killing. Running or hiding from such people is not in my DNA. I would rather die on my feet.

I saw real, ugly political violence in Jamaica. And if anyone wants a PhD in political violence, murder and gangsterism, spend a week in Haiti, where madness looks sane and death is an everyday event. A Lebanese-descended billionaire named Boulos, one of the richest men in Port-au-Prince, was arrested by the Americans last year, accused by the US government of a campaign of violence and gang support that helped destabilise Haiti. Another Lebanese billionaire up to no good in another black country on the other side of the planet. Boulos in Haiti. Boulos in Nigeria. Chagoury and the rest of them, welcomed into Africa with open arms, funding whatever is necessary to fuck us over wherever they can.

It is becoming boring and it is getting on my nerves.

And for those with short memories, let me remind you what was found in Kano in May 2013, because too many Nigerians have decided it was a footnote. It was not a footnote. It was an armoury.

After a month-long investigation, the army and the State Security Service broke through several layers of concrete under the master bedroom of a house owned by a Lebanese businessman in Kano. Packed into coolers and buried in sawdust they found eleven anti-tank weapons, four anti-tank mines, a rocket-propelled grenade launcher with twenty-one RPG rounds, seventeen AK-47 rifles, two sub-machine guns, seventy-six hand grenades, dynamite, and more than eleven thousand rounds of ammunition. Anti-tank mines. In a residential house. In Nigeria's largest northern city.

Three Lebanese nationals were arrested. One of them was caught at Kano airport trying to board a flight to Beirut with about sixty thousand dollars in cash. The security services said the men admitted to being trained by Hezbollah, and the SSS director in Kano stood in front of the cameras and called it exactly what it was: a Hezbollah cell and a Hezbollah armoury on Nigerian soil. The owner of the house was conveniently out of the country. The SSS also warned that a group like that could easily lend support to the local terrorists we already had on the ground, and this was at the height of Boko Haram.

Ask yourself who imported those weapons, who financed them, who cleared them through our ports and airports, and who looked the other way. Ask yourself whether that was the only house. And ask yourself why, thirteen years later, nobody in Abuja wants to talk about it.

It should alarm every Nigerian citizen that we are being managed by a handful of Arabs who care nothing for our welfare and do not respect our laws. Close one door on them and they will find another to open.

Let them arrest me. I am one of the best-connected Nigerians alive; my WhatsApp is a who's who of power. Let them try and see what happens. My report on Isabel dos Santos helped get an Interpol red notice placed on her, and she is Angolan-Russian. What do you think my connections will do if my own people try to be clever with me?

Nigerians need to stop being scared of their own shadows. It is becoming tiresome.

Kio Amachree

Traditionally prepared using ingredients such as rice, barley flour and sesame, depending on the custom, it is offered with the ancestor’s name, gotra and sankalp. It represents nourishment, gratitude and the family’s continuing responsibility towards those who came before.

The grains that sustain life become part of an offering for someone whose life helped shape the family performing the ritual.

Through the Sri Mandir app, devotees unable to travel can participate in priest-led Pinda Daan at participating sacred locations.

Welcome back, everyone to another edition of the latest movie news. 
“Avengers: Endgame--Encore,” the re-release of the 2019 Disney blockbuster, hit theaters this past weekend with new post-credit scenes and additional footage. The added material was enough to entice audiences and help the film open to $26 million and claim the No. 1 spot at the box office.

 “Resident Evil” landed in second place with $23 million followed by Paramount Pictures’ exciting survivalist thriller “Heart of the Beast” with $20 million. The film stars Brad Pitt, J.K. Simmons, Anna Lambe, and a beautiful German Shepherd named Uber/Odin. Overseas, “Heart of the Beast” collected a nifty $30.1 million.

A24’s psychological crime drama “Primetime,” starring Robert Pattinson, finished fourth ($19.1 million), and Universal Pictures/DreamWorks Animation’s delightful kid’s comedy, “Forgotten Island,” rounded out the Top Five with ($12.8 million). 

Here is what’s arriving in theaters on Oct. 2 and what I can’t wait to tell you about.

“VERITY” (In Theaters Oct. 2)—In the erotic thriller, “Verity,” struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh (Dakota Johnson, “Daddio” and Madame Web”) is offered a chance to take over a bestselling author’s unfinished series. She thinks she’s found her big break. But after arriving at the Crawford estate, Lowen discovers a disturbing manuscript that could expose secrets about Verity Crawford (Anne Hathaway, “The Devil Wears Prada 2”) and leave her questioning everything she’s been told by Verity’s husband, Jeremy Crawford (Josh Hartnett, “Trap” and “Oppenheimer”). 

“DIGGER” (In Theaters Oct. 2)—In this satirical black comedy, Tom Cruise stars as Digger Rockwell, a powerful and eccentric oil tycoon whose pursuit of control sets off a catastrophic chain of events that threatens the entire world. With disaster closing in, Digger launches a frantic mission to fix the crisis he helped create and convince everyone that he’s the one person who can save humanity. “Digger” also stars Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Jesse Plemons, Sandra Huller, and Michael Stuhlbarg. 

“NICKELS” (Opens In Select Theaters/And On Digital)-- In the drama “Nickels,” which is inspired by a true story, Rob Riggle stars as Tom Monroe, a man whose life is shaken when a young motorcycle accident victim sparks an unsettling connection to the brother he lost decades earlier. As Tom searches for an explanation, his daughter Harper (Odessa A'zion, TV’s “Stranger Things: Tales From ‘85”) finds herself caught up in a mystery that challenges everything their family believes about loss and faith.
 
I’ll have reviews of “Digger,” “Verity,” and “Nickels” posted to https://t.co/PaghpuwDiJ on Oct. 2. 

Be sure to join me for my movie review segment on the Kitty O'Neal Show Fridays at 5:17 p.m. and 6:47 p.m. on radio station KFBK 93.1 FM and 1530 AM.

Kimi Antonelli produced a breathtaking performance, after starting the race from P19, to overtake the rest of the pack and clinch the Italian Grand Prix victory in magnificent fashion on Sunday. This is how he did it! (Credit: Formula One)

News via Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One

Kimi Antonelli won Sunday’s Italian Grand Prix with team-mate George Russell P2.
It was a thrilling drive from Kimi as he charged through the field from P19 to become the first Italian to win their home race since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.
It also marks Mercedes 250th Grand Prix victory as a power unit manufacturer and the marque’s eighth victory at Monza; it’s first since 2018 at the ‘Temple of Speed’.

Starting out of position, Kimi started on the Hard tyre but was able to change to the Medium compound under an early race red flag. By that point, he had already gained seven places to run P12.

George meanwhile ran the conventional one-stop from P2 by starting on the Medium and taking the Hard under the red flag, with the clear goal to run to the end on that tyre as he led.

Kimi’s progressed continued once the race restarted and cycled through to battle his team-mate for the lead.

A mid-race Virtual Safety Car gave the team the option of pitting Kimi for a new Medium tyre, with signs suggesting that his original Medium tyre wouldn’t have the life to get to the end of the race.

He rejoined in P6 but made short work of cars ahead; in the final stages he closed the gap to George before making the pass for the lead with three laps left.

Our duo took the flag comfortably ahead of the rest of the field to secure the win, and the 50th for an Italian in F1.

Deputy Technical Director Simone Resta represented the team on the podium at his home race.

The team now leads the Constructors’ Championship by 122 points with Kimi heading the Drivers’ standings by 66 points from his team-mate George.

(Credit: Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One)

Profile

The Italian Grand Prix (Italian: Gran Premio d'Italia) is the fifth oldest national motor racing Grand Prix (after the French Grand Prix, the United States Grand Prix, the Spanish Grand Prix and the Russian Grand Prix), having been held since 1921. Since 2013, the Grand Prix has been held the most times, with 97 editions as of 2026.

It is one of the two Grands Prix (along with the British) which has run every season as an event of the Formula One World Championship Grands Prix, continuously since the championship was introduced in 1950.

Every Formula One Italian Grand Prix in the World Championship era has been held at Monza except in 1980, when it was held at Imola.

Profile

Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team

Mercedes-Benz, a German automotive brand of the Mercedes-Benz Group, has been involved in Formula One as both team owner and engine manufacturer for various periods since 1954. The current Mercedes-Benz Grand Prix Limited, competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, is based in Brackley, England, and holds a German racing licence. An announcement was made in December 2020 that Ineos planned to take a one third equal ownership stake alongside the Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff; this came into effect on 25 January 2022. Mercedes-branded teams are often referred to by the nickname, the "Silver Arrows" (German: Silberpfeile).

Formula 1 relocated the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix to Malaysia's Sepang track for October 2026, filling the slot left empty when Middle East conflicts canceled the original April race and shrank the season to 22 rounds. Bahrain covers the costs in this historic deal with Malaysia, slotting the event between Azerbaijan and Singapore races. Ferrari cheered the return, Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli called it 'so cool,' and Malaysia's Prime Minister praised the friendship, while fans note half the grid will experience Sepang for the first time amid its heat, rain, and challenging corners. What makes the Austrian Grand Prix special – and why you should see it

Discover what makes the F1 weekend in Austria unmissable.

The Austrian Grand Prix is a classic, and might just be held at one of the most picturesque track on the F1 calendar. Set in the Styrian hills, around 700m above sea level, the short track features rapid lap times and plenty of overtaking opportunities.

Despite the Red Bull Ring having the fewest corners of any circuit on the schedule, it's seen many unforgettable moments throughout the years – and, as the name might suggest, is the track that Red Bull calls home.

Let's take a look at just some of the reasons why Austria is so alluring.

Austrian racing heritage

Austria, despite it's relatively small population, has heaps of racing heritage. Triple World Champion Niki Lauda was born in Vienna, winning titles for Ferrari and McLaren, and was a major factor behind Mercedes’ success while helping convince Lewis Hamilton to join the outfit in 2013.

Jochen Rindt was Austria's first champion – the only posthumous F1 title winner, having tragically passed away during his dominant 1970 season. Gerhard Berger, while never taking the title himself, scored 10 wins during his illustrious career.

More recently, the late Austrian entrepreneur Dietrich Mateschitz and former Austrian F1 racer Helmut Marko – in his role as motorsport advisor – played key roles in Red Bull's success, with the team clinching eight Drivers’ and six Constructors’ titles.

When is the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix?

The 2026 Austrian Grand Prix weekend begins on Friday 26 June, with F1 cars hitting the track for the first two Free Practice sessions, before Free Practice 3 and Qualifying take place on Saturday 27 June. The Grand Prix itself is on Sunday 28 June, at 1500 local time.

Australian Grand Prix

The 2026 Australian Grand Prix is the season-opening race of the 2026 Formula 1 World Championship. It is currently taking place at the Albert Park Circuit in Melbourne from Friday, 6 March to Sunday, 8 March 2026.

Weekend Schedule

The event marks the beginning of a new era for F1, featuring overhauled technical regulations and the debut of the Cadillac team and Audi (via the Sauber takeover).

Friday, 6 March: Free Practice 1: 12:30 PM – 1:30 PM Free Practice 2: 4:00 PM – 5:00 PM
Saturday, 7 March: Free Practice 3: 12:30 PM – 1:30 PM Qualifying: 4:00 PM – 5:00 PM

Sunday, 8 March: Grand Prix (58 Laps): 3:00 PM Formula 1 +4

Event Highlights & Changes

New Teams & Drivers: Cadillac joins as the 11th team on the grid. New drivers include rookie Arvid Lindblad for Racing Bulls.

Pit Lane Speed Limit: Reduced from 80 km/h to 60 km/h for 2026 to accommodate the 11th team in the tight pit lane.

Infrastructure: A major $350 million redevelopment of the paddock and pit building is scheduled to begin immediately after this weekend's race.

Support Races: The weekend includes the season openers for Formula 2 and Formula 3, as well as the Supercars Championship.

Weather: Forecasts indicate mostly dry and bright conditions for the race on Sunday, with temperatures between 15°C and 24°C.

Viewing & Attendance

Broadcasting: In Australia, the race is live on Fox Sports (Channel 506), Kayo Sports, and free-to-air on Channel 10.

Tickets: Most tickets for the event sold out quickly after going on sale in September 2025. Fans are warned to only use official channels like https://t.co/xIEKhxv3jE to avoid scams.

Formula 1 released a 57-second high-energy video showcasing the full 2026 grid in dynamic poses, team liveries, and dramatic effects, timed for this weekend's Australian Grand Prix. Reigning champion Lando Norris leads for McLaren alongside Oscar Piastri, with Mercedes' George Russell leaning sleekly—farewell to his famous T-pose—and rookie Kimi Antonelli earning solo hype. Highlights include Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc for Ferrari, Max Verstappen with Isack Hadjar at Red Bull, and newcomers like Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, building excitement for the new regs with smaller cars and sustainable fuels.

Verstappen Slams 2026 F1 Cars as Formula E on Steroids

Charles Leclerc topped timesheets with a 1:34.273 lap for Ferrari on day two of F1's first pre-season test, ahead of Lando Norris's P2 and Haas rookie Oliver Bearman's strong P3.

The new 2026 rules bring smaller chassis, active aero, and power units with nearly 50% electric power, tightening lap times around 1:34 but drawing fire from Verstappen over heavy energy management he calls anti-racing. Norris urged drivers to stop whining, while Lewis Hamilton found them fun yet ridiculously complex; Red Bull hit technical snags, Mercedes engine issues, and three more test days remain before the March 7-9 opener.

Kimi Antonelli won Sunday’s Italian Grand Prix with team-mate George Russell P2.

It was a thrilling drive from Kimi as he charged through the field from P19 to become the first Italian to win their home race since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

It also marks Mercedes 250th Grand Prix victory as a power unit manufacturer and the marque’s eighth victory at Monza; it’s first since 2018 at the ‘Temple of Speed’.

Starting out of position, Kimi started on the Hard tyre but was able to change to the Medium compound under an early race red flag. By that point, he had already gained seven places to run P12.

George meanwhile ran the conventional one-stop from P2 by starting on the Medium and taking the Hard under the red flag, with the clear goal to run to the end on that tyre as he led.

Kimi’s progressed continued once the race restarted and cycled through to battle his team-mate for the lead.

A mid-race Virtual Safety Car gave the team the option of pitting Kimi for a new Medium tyre, with signs suggesting that his original Medium tyre wouldn’t have the life to get to the end of the race.

He rejoined in P6 but made short work of cars ahead; in the final stages he closed the gap to George before making the pass for the lead with three laps left.

Our duo took the flag comfortably ahead of the rest of the field to secure the win, and the 50th for an Italian in F1.

Deputy Technical Director Simone Resta represented the team on the podium at his home race.

The team now leads the Constructors’ Championship by 122 points with Kimi heading the Drivers’ standings by 66 points from his team-mate George.

What makes the Austrian Grand Prix special – and why you should see it

Discover what makes the F1 weekend in Austria unmissable.

The Austrian Grand Prix is a classic, and might just be held at one of the most picturesque track on the F1 calendar. Set in the Styrian hills, around 700m above sea level, the short track features rapid lap times and plenty of overtaking opportunities.

Despite the Red Bull Ring having the fewest corners of any circuit on the schedule, it's seen many unforgettable moments throughout the years – and, as the name might suggest, is the track that Red Bull calls home.

Let's take a look at just some of the reasons why Austria is so alluring.

Austrian racing heritage

Austria, despite it's relatively small population, has heaps of racing heritage. Triple World Champion Niki Lauda was born in Vienna, winning titles for Ferrari and McLaren, and was a major factor behind Mercedes’ success while helping convince Lewis Hamilton to join the outfit in 2013.

Jochen Rindt was Austria's first champion – the only posthumous F1 title winner, having tragically passed away during his dominant 1970 season. Gerhard Berger, while never taking the title himself, scored 10 wins during his illustrious career.

More recently, the late Austrian entrepreneur Dietrich Mateschitz and former Austrian F1 racer Helmut Marko – in his role as motorsport advisor – played key roles in Red Bull's success, with the team clinching eight Drivers’ and six Constructors’ titles.

When is the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix?

The 2026 Austrian Grand Prix weekend begins on Friday 26 June, with F1 cars hitting the track for the first two Free Practice sessions, before Free Practice 3 and Qualifying take place on Saturday 27 June. The Grand Prix itself is on Sunday 28 June, at 1500 local time.
