text:
🕸️👧🏾 Sjoe! The Safety Net Has Holes — And Children Are Falling Through ~ 💔💰 The Grants Arrive. The Protection Doesn’t ~ 👧🏾⚠️ Sjoe! 17,000 Children Later, the Safety Net Is Still Fraying.
The Boksburg Kidz Clinic has assisted more than 17 000 abused children and their parents over twenty-five years. Since March 2026 it has received no expected funding from the Gauteng Department of Social Development.

Social workers continue assessments, therapy and court preparation.

Salaries do not. The organisation is drawing on reserves it cannot stretch indefinitely. Official statements refer to an “incorrect programme” application and administrative compliance still being finalised.

Similar accounts have appeared across Gauteng for four consecutive financial years. Non-profit organisations that deliver core child-protection work wait months for Service Level Agreements or payments.

Some close permanently.

Cases transfer to already overloaded government social workers. In previous cycles unspent funds have been returned to Treasury while services contracted.

This is not a temporary administrative hiccup. It is the latest expression of a century-long pattern in which specialised protection for the children who need it most remains the most fragile layer of the welfare net.

Grants reach millions of households. The professional capacity that turns rights into safety does not. History is unambiguous about what follows when that layer continues to thin.

1. South Africa’s Long Shadow: Child Protection After a Century of Uneven Care

The 1913 Children’s Protection Act brought the state into child welfare. In practice it served mainly white children. Black and coloured children relied on family networks or mission societies. When the 1918 Spanish Flu killed an estimated 300 000 to 350 000 South Africans within weeks, the design became visible. Approximately twenty new orphanages opened; nearly all catered for white children.

The majority of orphans were absorbed by extended families or left with minimal formal support (Phillips, 1984/2018).

Post-1994 legislation removed formal racial barriers. The Children’s Act 2005 and the expansion of the Child Support Grant created a rights-based framework that now reaches millions. Yet the delivery of specialised services—risk assessment, trauma therapy, court preparation, emergency protection—still depends heavily on provincially funded non-profits.

Those payments arrive late, partially, or not at all.

The Boksburg clinic and dozens of parallel cases in 2024, 2025 and 2026 demonstrate continuity: durable, universal frontline capacity for intensive intervention has never been constructed.

Grants function.

The professional layer that converts grants and rights into actual protection remains intermittently funded and therefore chronically fragile (Chisholm, 1990; South African Child Gauge series).

The pattern is structural. Specialised services erode first under fiscal or administrative pressure precisely because they were never built as robust, permanent public capacity.

A rights-based system that cannot reliably fund the specialists who make rights real is a system still operating inside its original design constraints.

Sjoe!
A state that can return unspent millions to Treasury while a clinic that has served 17 000 children operates without salaries is not short of money. It is short of the administrative will to treat specialised protection as non-negotiable infrastructure rather than a residual line item.

Questions Stirring:
Why has a constitutional rights framework still not produced reliable professional capacity for the children who need intensive support?
What does the repeated return of unspent funds while services close reveal about actual rather than declared priorities?
If the design flaw is a century old, what would durable frontline capacity require in the present fiscal and administrative environment?

These questions matter because they move the story from “there isn't enough money” to the much harder question of what the system actually does with the money, capacity and constitutional obligations it has.

2. When the Safety Net Thins: Children, Poverty and the Limits of Grants Alone

When specialised protection capacity contracts, extended family eventually reaches its limit. Children then overflow into streets or low-quality institutions. The sequence is historically consistent.

After war and famine in early Soviet Russia, millions of besprizornye lived on the streets or in overwhelmed homes. In late-Ceaușescu and post-1989 Romania, austerity and institutional collapse produced both high mortality inside orphanages and later street populations.

Industrialising America and the Great Depression generated large numbers of homeless and migrant children. South Africa has not reached those absolute scales.

The mechanism is nevertheless operating.

Permanent non-profit closures, case transfers to stretched government social workers, and child poverty rates that remain higher than in 2019 are already thinning the specialised layer that previously absorbed many high-risk cases (GroundUp reporting 2024–2026; South African Child Gauge).

Cash grants still reach millions and prevent some destitution. They do not assess risk, prepare a child for court, or provide therapeutic support after abuse. Grants alone have never been sufficient to prevent the residual outcomes that appear when the professional layer disappears.

The quiet danger is that grant coverage can continue to look impressive on paper while the protective capacity that keeps children out of the historical overflow steadily contracts.

Progress measured solely by grant numbers can therefore mask the erosion that matters most for the highest-risk children.

Sjoe!
It is possible to celebrate the reach of cash transfers while the very services that stop a child from needing those transfers in the first place are allowed to wither. The arithmetic is tidy. The outcomes are not.

Questions Stirring:
At what point does the thinning of specialised services begin to increase measurable street or institutional numbers even while grant coverage remains broad?
How many children previously supported by closed or suspended non-profits are now receiving equivalent professional attention?
What independent data exist on outcomes for cases transferred from non-profits to provincial social workers?

These questions matter because they expose a second-order problem: a social-protection system can look strong on the balance sheet while the specialised services underneath it quietly weaken.

3. Beyond Annual Crisis: Rebuilding Reliable Protection for South Africa’s Children

Across successive Gauteng MECs the annual sequence has remained constant: late or incomplete Service Level Agreements, partial quarterly payments, compliance disputes, organisational strain, protests, court interventions or mediation, and partial catch-up that fails to prevent the next year’s repetition.

The problem is embedded in budgeting rules, compliance systems, prioritisation and administrative capacity. Personnel changes have not altered the loop.

Historically, specialised services for the majority of children have been treated as residual and therefore dispensable under pressure—whether under segregation, apartheid resource allocation, or post-apartheid provincial administration.

Democratic institutions have reproduced the outcome: when resources tighten, the services that protect the most vulnerable are delayed or reduced first. The continuity across leadership cycles demonstrates that the crisis is structural. Only redesign of the mechanisms that repeatedly produce the same disruption can change the pattern.

Court orders and mediation have produced temporary relief. They have not broken the annual ritual. That fact itself is evidence. When external pressure yields only partial and temporary compliance, the underlying rules remain the decisive variable.

Sjoe!
Four years of the same sequence, multiple leadership changes, court papers, mediation and protests, and the ritual continues with only minor variations in the script. At some point the word “malfunction” becomes a polite way of describing policy.

Questions Stirring:
Which specific budgeting and compliance rules produce the same annual delay regardless of who holds the MEC post?
What accountability measures have been applied, if any, when unspent funds are returned while services close?
If court orders and mediation have not broken the cycle, what stronger institutional redesign is required?

These questions matter because they move the story from “another year, another crisis” to the much harder question: why does the same failure keep reproducing itself?

4. The Annual Ritual of Almost-Funding

Every financial year the performance unfolds with remarkable consistency. Business plans are submitted months in advance. The budget is finalised. Organisations wait. Some receive contracts containing errors.

Others wait for formal rejection letters that never arrive, thereby blocking appeals. Payments trickle out weeks or months late. Staff go unpaid. Services shrink. Protests occur. Court papers are filed or mediation is attempted.

Partial payments eventually flow for many. The next cycle begins.

In 2026 the pattern continued. The Gauteng Care Crisis Committee reported hundreds of jobs and thousands of beneficiaries at risk months into the year. One registered child-protection organisation permanently ceased operations.

The Boksburg clinic remained without its expected tranche. Official statements noted that compliant organisations with signed agreements are paid and that remaining cases involve compliance or application issues.

The ritual itself continues uninterrupted.

The predictability is the most telling feature. When the same sequence recurs despite changes in leadership, external legal pressure and public protest, the sequence is no longer an accident. It is the system operating as designed.

Sjoe!
There is a peculiar administrative genius in a process that can generate the identical crisis four years running while still describing each year’s version as an unfortunate exception requiring further engagement.

Questions Stirring:
How many consecutive years of the same sequence are required before the pattern is treated as policy rather than malfunction?
What is the cumulative loss of organisational knowledge and community trust when centres close or operate under permanent uncertainty?
Why does a system capable of returning unspent funds find it so difficult to pay the organisations already delivering the services those funds were allocated for?

These questions matter because they move the argument from “something went wrong again” to “what is the accumulated effect of a system that repeatedly produces the same problem?”

5. History’s Quiet Warning: What Happens When the Specialists Disappear

Major historical surges in unsupported children combined two pressures: a rise in family incapacity and a simultaneous contraction of formal protection capacity. South Africa now faces a milder but structurally analogous combination.

Child poverty remains elevated relative to 2019 while the non-profit layer that supplies therapy, court preparation and emergency protection continues to shrink through funding delays and closures.

Historical recovery patterns are equally clear. Emergency institutions without family support left residual street and institutional populations. Cash support without functioning investigation, therapy and placement capacity failed in the same way.

Sustainable improvement required both: income measures that enabled families to keep children, and professional services that could intervene when families could not.

South Africa currently maintains relatively broad grant coverage while permitting the specialised infrastructure to erode. Grants cannot assess risk or prepare a child for court. Specialised services cannot address the poverty that drives many placements.

Both must function reliably and at adequate real value.

The dual requirement is not a preference. It is the only combination that has historically reversed the overflow trajectory. Single-lever solutions—more institutions alone or more cash alone—have consistently left large residual populations of unsupported children.

Sjoe!
History does not offer a third option in which one can indefinitely thin the professional layer while expanding cash transfers and still avoid the residual outcomes. The record is stubborn on this point.

Questions Stirring:
What would simultaneous stabilisation of real-value grants and reliable frontline professional capacity actually cost and require administratively?
Which historical recoveries offer the most transferable lessons for a middle-income country with existing grant infrastructure?
If the dual restoration is not pursued, how long before the quieter overflow of unsupported children becomes statistically undeniable?

These questions matter because they push the argument beyond “grants versus services” and toward the harder question of whether a functioning social-protection system needs both.

The Net and the Price

The strands converge. The fragility of specialised child protection is the latest expression of a century-long design that never built durable capacity for the children who need intensive intervention. Grants have expanded. The professional layer that converts rights into safety continues to thin under repeated administrative failure.

Independent lines of evidence—legislative history, comparative cases of welfare collapse and recovery, contemporary funding data, and post-COVID poverty trends—point to the same conclusion: elevated need meeting shrinking specialised capacity precedes the residual outcomes of street children and inadequate institutions.

The path forward is therefore not another annual funding scramble or a false choice between cash and services. It is the simultaneous stabilisation of both.

Until the net is made reliable at both layers, the forgotten children will remain those for whom the system’s incomplete design still extracts the highest price.

The cumulative evidence—from a century of South African legislative and administrative history, comparative international cases, contemporary provincial funding records, and post-COVID poverty data—establishes that specialised child-protection capacity remains structurally fragile and that dual restoration of family income support and reliable frontline services is the only historically validated route to preventing deeper residual harm.

The Church today is not Israel under the Mosaic covenant, and salvation is not earned by keeping Israel’s statutes. The believer is saved “by grace…through faith” and “not of works” (Ephesians 2:8–9). Yet grace does not produce contempt for obedience. Jesus said, “If ye love me, keep my commandments” (John 14:15). Obedience is not payment for Calvary; the blood of Christ cannot be reimbursed. It is the proper response of one who has been freely redeemed. The Christian who constantly asks how little obedience he can offer while still claiming love for Christ has already exposed what interests him most. Love does not calculate the minimum acceptable amount of loyalty.

2. Eyewitness Privilege Creates Eyewitness Responsibility

Moses distinguishes the present hearers from “your children which have not known, and which have not seen.” That difference is not accidental. Scripture repeatedly teaches that light increases accountability. Luke 12:48 states the principle plainly: “For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required.” Greater privilege is not spiritual padding around a man that softens judgment. It increases responsibility. The person standing beneath a floodlight has less excuse for stumbling over what someone in darkness could not see. Israel’s experiences had flooded the road with light. They had been given divine demonstrations few generations would ever witness so directly.

Privilege becomes dangerous when familiarity produces contempt. Manna eventually became ordinary breakfast. The pillar of cloud could become scenery. Miracles repeated often enough could begin to feel normal. Fallen flesh has an astonishing capacity to turn wonders into wallpaper. Moses therefore keeps reopening Israel’s memory because God’s greatness had not diminished merely because Israel had grown accustomed to it. The Red Sea did not become less miraculous after the tenth retelling. Divine provision did not become less gracious because it arrived every morning. Familiarity should deepen gratitude. Instead, the flesh often treats repeated blessing as entitlement and then becomes offended when the next demand is not immediately satisfied.

The same principle applies whenever men receive unusual access to biblical truth. A child raised beneath sound preaching and Scripture has received a tremendous privilege. A believer who has spent thirty years studying the Bible cannot plead the ignorance of a new convert. A congregation that has heard line upon line of clear doctrine possesses light many churches have never enjoyed. Knowledge is stewardship. The man who knows twenty doctrines and obeys none of them is not spiritually wealthy; he is carrying twenty witnesses against his disobedience. Bible knowledge was never intended merely to make a Christian more impressive in discussion. Light was given so he could see where to walk.

3. They Saw What God Did to Egypt

Moses recalls “his miracles, and his acts, which he did in the midst of Egypt unto Pharaoh the king of Egypt, and unto all his land” (Deuteronomy 11:3). Israel’s deliverance from Egypt had not come through military strategy or diplomatic pressure. Pharaoh controlled the throne, the army, the chariots, and the visible machinery of power. Israel possessed bricks, burdens, bruised backs, and groaning. Then the LORD entered the contest openly. The plagues were not unfortunate weather patterns arriving in inconvenient sequence. They were judgments. Pharaoh had asked, “Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice?” (Exodus 5:2). God answered him until Egypt understood that a king wearing a crown is still only dust when the Almighty rises to judge.

#Fascismloveaffair

The romanticism around Germany’s “rebuilding years” is extraordinary. Germany did not simply suffer a tragedy that fell from the sky.

 Germany started two world wars, carried out genocide, devastated Europe and peoples under European fascism in the so-called colonies, and helped produce destruction on a global scale.

Then it was rebuilt by the United States through the Marshall Plan — a country whose own wealth was built on Indigenous dispossession, slavery, racial capitalism, and empire. Black Americans fought in the war against Nazi Germany, only to return home to Jim Crow, segregation, lynching, voter suppression, and second-class citizenship. 

That is the joke at the centre of this story: Germany was reconstructed as a civilised Western partner, while the descendants of enslaved people who helped defeat fascism were denied basic dignity at home. 

So no, Germany’s rebuilding cannot be told as a sentimental story of rubble, discipline, and resilience.

It was also white supremacy rewarding white colonising 
Europe with reconstruction, forgiveness, and reintegration — while colonised and racialised peoples were left with debt, occupation, extraction, and lectures on responsibility.

The rest of the world was never offered that kind of mercy — and that is why we are reliving fascism in 2026: because the world continues to tell selective stories about violence, guilt, reconstruction, and who deserves forgiveness.

The war had ended. The rebuilding had only begun.

In 1945, many German cities were landscapes of ruins. Homes, bridges, railways and entire neighborhoods had been destroyed, while everyday life had to continue through shortages, displacement and uncertainty.

Then came the long work of rebuilding. Street by street, rubble was cleared. Homes reopened, transport returned, and cities slowly began to live again.

For many German families, this was not simply history — it was part of their own story.

Did you, your parents, or your grandparents ever tell stories about Germany’s rebuilding years after 1945?

As a business owner, you can post content daily, send 100 outreach messages a day, run a thousand different ads across multiple platforms...

And still not sign a SINGLE client.

When that happens, I suggest you give your offer a look before anything else.

I can speak for the companies I help, in Bitcoin, fintech and advisory: buyers usually need to be educated before they buy.

And there it mostly comes down to two things.

> How painful is the problem you solve?

> And how urgent is it for them, right now? Urgent as in, an actual priority.

What surprised me is that: pain alone IS NOT enough.

I learned this one with my own Bitcoin consulting.

I got much more interest from European and Gulf markets than from Lebanon, and Lebanon is where people needed Bitcoin the MOST.

People here watched banks freeze their accounts, and their savings with them. The pain can't get more real 😅

Yet for many people I talked to, it still wasn't a priority.

> When you're not even making money, protecting it isn't what you wake up thinking about.

So the pain was there, but the urgency wasn't.

Now, 100 messages a day and daily content won't fix an offer like that.

But they will help you properly know if your offer is any good. You'll know pretty fast from how people react to it.

That's assuming you're articulating what you offer clearly... I'm not saying to use copywriting gimmicks, just a simple offer explanation in your content / outreach.

Honestly, you can think about that offer for weeks, in strategy sessions, thinking sessions, frameworks.

These certainly help, and I use them too. (Hormozi's Value Equation is amazing... and I revert to it frequently..)

But nothing tells you more than the market's answer.

Testing your offer against the market is absolutely unbeatable.

P.S. Not just testing, but adapting to the market's needs, or changing markets, or changing offers...

→ How do you test your offers? And what did the market end up teaching you? Curious to read it below.

Louis-Alexandre Berthier, prince de Neuchâtel et Valangin, prince de Wagram (English: /ˈbɜːrtieɪ/ BUR-tee-ay, French: [lwi alɛksɑ̃dʁ bɛʁtje]; 20 November 1753 – 1 June 1815) was a French military commander who served during the French Revolutionary Wars and the Napoleonic Wars. He was twice Minister of War of France and was made a Marshal of the Empire in 1804. Berthier served as chief of staff to Napoleon Bonaparte from his first Italian campaign in 1796 until his first abdication in 1814. The operational efficiency of the Grande Armée owed much to his considerable administrative and organizational skills.

Born into a military family, Berthier served in the American Revolutionary War and survived suspicion of monarchism during the Reign of Terror before a rapid rise in the ranks of the French Revolutionary Army. Although a key supporter of the coup against the Directory that gave Napoleon supreme power, and present for his greatest victories, Berthier strongly opposed the progressive stretching of lines of communication during the Russian campaign. Allowed to retire by the restored Bourbon regime, he died by either suicide or murder shortly before the Battle of Waterloo. Berthier's reputation as a superb operational organiser remains strong among current historians.

Berthier was born in Versailles on 20 November 1753.[1] He was the eldest of five surviving children of Lieutenant-Colonel Jean-Baptiste Berthier (1721–1804), an officer in the Corps of Topographical Engineers, and his first wife (married in 1746) Marie Françoise L'Huillier de La Serre.[2] Three of his brothers also served in the French Army, with two, César (1765–1819) and Victor-Léopold (1770–1807), becoming generals during the Napoleonic Wars.[2][3]

Early career
As a boy, Berthier was instructed in the military art by his father, an officer of the Corps de genie (Engineer Corps). In 1764 he was admitted to the Royal Engineering School of Mézières, as a second lieutenant, graduating as a topographical engineer two years later, at the age of 12.[2] In March 1772, Berthier entered the army as a lieutenant in the Flanders Legion.[2] He then joined the Prince of Lambesc's Lorraine Dragoon Regiment in August 1776, and was promoted to captain in June 1777.[2]

Berthier first saw action during the American Revolutionary War, in which he served from 1780 to 1783 as a staff officer under Jean-Baptiste Donatien de Vimeur, Count of Rochambeau.[2] On his return, having attained the rank of colonel, he was employed in various staff posts and was made a Knight of Saint Louis in 1788.[2] In July 1789, at the start of the French Revolution, Berthier was made a lieutenant-colonel as well as chief of staff of the Versailles National Guard, and in this role protected King Louis XVI's family from popular violence.[2] In 1791, he aided in the emigration of the king's aunts Victoire and Adélaïde.[1][2]

French Revolutionary Wars
In 1792, Berthier was promoted to maréchal de camp and posted to the Army of the North.[2] He was appointed chief of staff to Marshal Nicolas Luckner, and played a distinguished part in the Argonne campaign of Generals Dumouriez and Kellermann. He served with great credit in the War in the Vendée of 1793–1796. Berthier was made a brigade general in March 1795 and a general of division three months later.[2]

Berthier first met Napoleon Bonaparte, when he was a general in March 1796, and was at once made chief of staff to the Army of Italy, which Bonaparte had recently been appointed to command.[2] He served in the Italian campaign of 1796, distinguishing himself at the Battle of Lodi.[2] In January 1797 he played an important role in the Battle of Rivoli, relieving General Joubert when the latter was attacked by the Austrian general Jozsef Alvinczi. His power of work, accuracy and quick comprehension, combined with his long and varied experience and his complete mastery of detail, made Berthier the ideal chief of staff. In this capacity, Berthier was Napoleon's most valued assistant for the rest of his career.[1]

Berthier accompanied Napoleon throughout the campaign of 1797, and was left in charge of the army after the Treaty of Campo Formio. He was in this post in 1798 when he entered Italy, INVADED THE VATICAN, ORGANIZED THE ROMAN REPUBLIC, AND TOOK POPE PIUS VI PRISONER. text:
I sit in the dark gaming chair after the red light vanishes from the camera lens.

The room drops into silence in less than a second.

My ears ring from two hours of shouting at a small piece of glass mounted on a tripod.

On the desk in front of me, three wide monitor screens fade to black, ending the live feed that was just broadcasting my face to over 100,000 people at once.

When I say that millions of people know Speed but almost nobody knows Darren, I usually think of it as a tragic mistake.

I tell myself that there’s a quiet young man named Darren who gets lost behind a loud, chaotic character named Speed.

I picture Speed as a mask I put on at the start of a stream and take off at the end.

But sitting here in the dark, watching my hands still tremble from leftover adrenaline, I realise that simple explanation fails.

The camera didn't create the chaos out of nothing.

It demanded energy, and I supplied it from my own body.

What’s the machine on my desk actually doing?

It takes physical movements, shouts, muscle twitches, and emotional surges, compresses them into digital signals, and sends them across the world to millions of glowing rectangular screens.

People sit in their bedrooms, on buses, or at school, watching that small rectangle.

They see a young man jumping over furniture, shouting at video games, barking at strangers, and reacting with extreme intensity to every tiny event.

To them, that stream of movement is Speed.

It’s high energy, highly volatile, and completely unpredictable.

The viewer wants an event.

A person is slow and inefficient when they aren't performing.

A real person gets tired, becomes quiet, thinks silently, changes his mind, or simply sits in silence for ten minutes.

If I sat quietly on stream for ten minutes, the viewer counter on the screen would begin to drop.

Tens of thousands of people would click away to find another glowing rectangle offering immediate stimulation.

The algorithm that distributes my face rewards non stop motion and punishes rest.

So I optimised the output.

I trained myself to turn every internal impulse into an explosive external action.

I built an engine that converts my own vitality into digital attention at maximum velocity.

Where does that leave Darren?

I used to believe Darren was a separate person waiting behind the curtain, waiting for the stream to end so he could exist.

But when the stream ends, there isn't a separate person waiting.

There’s only an exhausted 21 year old young man sitting alone in a silent room, emptied of all the energy he spent over the last three hours.

Why does hyper visibility feel like total isolation?

The problem isn't that people refuse to see Darren.

The problem is that the structure of live broadcasting makes mutual seeing impossible.

True connection requires two way recognition.

It requires two people looking at each other in the same physical space, adjusting their tone, reading subtle facial shifts, and sharing quiet moments.

On a live broadcast with 100,000 active viewers, the text chat moves so fast that it becomes a continuous blur of coloured symbols and short words.

I can't read individual thoughts.

I'm not conversing with individual people; I'm steering a massive wave of collective emotion.

The wave responds to excitement, outrage, and shock.

The wave can't offer companionship because a crowd is an environment, not a friend.

I complain that people only care about Speed, but I'm the one who built Speed to replace the slower, more vulnerable parts of myself.

Speed is safe because Speed can't be rejected for who he is.

Speed is evaluated purely on performance, like an engine or an athlete.

If the performance is loud enough, the audience stays.

If I show up as Darren, quiet, uncertain, and ordinary, the audience leaves.

I traded the slow, difficult work of building personal relationships for the instant, massive feedback of public attention.

Attention feels like love from a distance, but it behaves differently when you try to live inside it.

Attention is a light that shines on you, not a hand that holds you.

When the light goes out, it leaves the room darker than it was before.

The isolation I feel when I wake up isn't an accident or a misunderstanding by my fans.

It’s the natural consequence of how the system operates.

I built a digital spectacle that requires all my life force to stay lit, and then I'm surprised when I've no life force left for myself.

The millions of people watching don't know Darren because Darren is the fuel that gets burned to keep Speed glowing on their screens.

You can't burn your life for fuel and expect to keep it at the same time.

My real name is Darren Jason Watkins Jr., better known as IShowSpeed or simply Speed.

text:
Prompt video 1 :

SCENE CONTEXT
Create a 30-second, 1080p ultra-realistic personal home video capturing a quiet, heartbreaking encounter in an older Seoul neighborhood. A beautiful young Korean woman, exhausted and hungry, sits outside a small convenience store. A young Korean man notices her and shares his food. Her restrained reaction carries the emotion: embarrassment, disbelief, then relief at being treated kindly.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
Text-only generation. The written descriptions define the consistent characters, objects, and locations throughout.

CHARACTERS
Woman: Korean, 23, naturally beautiful, pale tired face, slightly chapped lips, long black hair loosely tied back with stray strands around her cheeks. Worn beige cardigan over a plain gray shirt, faded blue jeans, scuffed white sneakers. Natural skin texture, no glamorous makeup. She moves slowly and avoids eye contact, trying to hide her hunger.

Man: Korean, 26, short black hair, gentle expression, navy windbreaker, white T-shirt, dark trousers, gray sneakers. His concern is expressed through patient, ordinary gestures.

His off-screen friend holds the camcorder, initially recording their walk.

ENVIRONMENT
An older Seoul residential alley on a cool, overcast afternoon. A small convenience store faces the pavement; a weathered wooden bench stands beside its entrance, with a red-brick wall behind it. The woman sits at the left end. The man approaches from the right carrying one small transparent shopping bag containing one wrapped bread roll and one sealed water bottle. Soft daylight, distant neighborhood traffic, a faint refrigerator hum from the open store entrance.

CAMERA & TEXTURE
Raw early-2000s consumer DV footage filmed by a friend: strong natural handheld shake, spontaneous imperfect framing, occasional autofocus hunting, exposure shifts, motion blur, faded colors, soft digital detail, mild noise, and brief accidental zooms. The camera follows the activity with natural amateur movements.

The friend begins one step behind the man, then stops near the bench’s right end, leaving the woman space. Walking creates visible footstep shake. When the man stops unexpectedly, the camera briefly drifts past him before correcting. Later details are captured with one hesitant short zoom. Keep the interaction readable and quietly observed.

FORMAT MODE
Five timed home-video segments with exact hard cuts at 6, 12, 18, and 24 seconds. End at exactly 30 seconds. Preserve the same bench, character positions, clothing, food, and bag across cuts.

ACTION & TIMING
0–6 seconds:
The camera follows behind the man approaching the store. On the bench, the woman searches an empty cardigan pocket, then lowers her hand into her lap. She notices the bread through his shopping bag; her gaze lingers before she quickly looks down, embarrassed. He notices and stops. The operator takes one extra step, then corrects the framing.

6–12 seconds:
From beside the bench, a slightly crooked medium shot. The man bends his knees to meet her eye level without crowding her. Holding the bag in his left hand, he retrieves the wrapped bread with his right and gently offers it.
He quietly says in Korean, “이거 드세요.”
She looks from the bread to his face, hesitating, then accepts it with both hands. He releases it only once her grip is secure.

12–18 seconds:
The man sits at the bench’s right end, leaving a respectful gap. He places the bag on the bench to his right, removes the sealed water bottle, and sets it upright between them.
The woman rests the bread on her lap and peels back the wrapper with trembling fingers. The camera makes a small imperfect zoom toward her hands; autofocus briefly searches, then settles. She lifts the partially wrapped bread and takes one small bite.

18–24 seconds:
A closer, imperfectly framed view of her face. She chews slowly and swallows. Her shoulders loosen, but her eyes fill with tears. She pauses with the bread held over her lap, presses her lips together, and wipes one cheek with her free hand.
In a barely steady voice, she says, “감사합니다.”
The camera holds quietly, with subtle hand tremor.

24–30 seconds:
A wider view includes both of them. He gives a small reassuring nod and says softly, “천천히 드세요.”
He then looks toward the alley, giving her privacy. She takes another small bite, holding the wrapper beneath the bread to catch crumbs. Her gaze drops, tears still visible, but her breathing settles. End on both sitting quietly together, the untouched water bottle standing between them.

AUDIO
Natural Korean dialogue only as specified. Distant passing vehicles, faint footsteps, refrigerator hum, bread-wrapper rustling, quiet breathing, and subtle camcorder-handling noise. Her voice is fragile and restrained; his voice is gentle and conversational. No background music or narration.

CONTINUITY
Maintain consistent faces, ages, hairstyles, clothing, and footwear. One bread roll transfers from the man’s bag to the woman and remains partially wrapped; each bite visibly reduces it. One water bottle remains sealed and upright between them. The shopping bag stays at the man’s right after being placed there. Preserve realistic hands, chewing, swallowing, restrained tears, and the bench’s geography. Use ordinary overcast daylight throughout. Fully photorealistic live action; no stylized lighting, slow motion, beauty filters, subtitles, added text, logos, or watermark.

Here are the scriptures mentioned written out so you don't have to go find them.

A simple way to use them: read one passage, then say, “Lord, I receive this in Jesus’ name for myself and my household.”  

Here they are in the King James Version. You can read them aloud as prayer.

### Psalm 91
He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.  
I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.  
Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.  
He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.  
Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day;  
Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.  
A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.  
Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.  
Because thou hast made the Lord, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation;  
There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling.  
For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.  
They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.  
Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet.  
Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.  
He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him.  
With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation.

### Psalm 23
The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.  
He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.  
He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.  
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.  
Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.  
Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.

### Psalm 27
The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the Lord is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?  
When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes, came upon me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell.  
Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.  
One thing have I desired of the Lord, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to enquire in his temple.  
For in the time of trouble he shall hide me in his pavilion: in the secret of his tabernacle shall he hide me; he shall set me up upon a rock.  
And now shall mine head be lifted up above mine enemies round about me: therefore will I offer in his tabernacle sacrifices of joy; I will sing, yea, I will sing praises unto the Lord.  
Hear, O Lord, when I cry with my voice: have mercy also upon me, and answer me.  
When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, Thy face, Lord, will I seek.  
Hide not thy face far from me; put not thy servant away in anger: thou hast been my help; leave me not, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation.  
When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take me up.  
Teach me thy way, O Lord, and lead me in a plain path, because of mine enemies.  
Deliver me not over unto the will of mine enemies: for false witnesses are risen up against me, and such as breathe out cruelty.  
I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.  
Wait on the Lord: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the Lord.

### Psalm 121
I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.  
My help cometh from the Lord, which made heaven and earth.  
He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber.

The Lord is thy keeper: the Lord is thy shade upon thy right hand.

text:
Prayers to help in spiritual warfare to say for yourself and for Nicki. 

**The Lord’s Prayer**  
Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.

“Deliver us from evil” is the core petition.

### 2. Renounce and claim covering
Many Christians pray something like this (adapt the wording to your tradition):

> Lord Jesus Christ, I belong to you. You bought me with your blood. I reject every curse, spell, *trabajo*, *bilongo*, or word spoken against me from any source—human or demonic. I cancel their claim in your name. I forgive those who meant me harm. I put on the armor of God. Cover my mind, body, home, family, and possessions with your blood. No weapon formed against me shall prosper. Amen.

That last line is from Isaiah 54:17.

### 3. Scripture people pray aloud
These are often read as prayer, not just study:

- **Psalm 91** — dwelling in God’s shelter; “no evil shall befall you”
- **Psalm 23** — the Lord as shepherd; “I will fear no evil”
- **Psalm 27** — “The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?”
- **Psalm 121** — help from the Maker of heaven and earth
- **Ephesians 6:10–18** — the armor of God
- **Colossians 2:14–15** — Christ disarming powers and authorities
- **Luke 10:19** — authority over the enemy 
- **1 John 4:4** — “greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world”
- **Galatians 3:13** — Christ became a curse for us, so those in Him are not under corruption’s curse

A simple way to use them: read the psalm slowly, then say, “Father, apply this to me and my household in Jesus’ name.”

### 4. St. Michael (widely used by Catholics; many Protestants also use it)

> Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle. Be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the devil. May God rebuke him, we humbly pray; and do thou, O Prince of the heavenly host, by the power of God, cast into hell Satan and all the evil spirits who prowl about the world seeking the ruin of souls. Amen.

Catholics may also use holy water in the home, the Sign of the Cross, and the Rosary; those are sacramentals.

### 5. A short daily protection prayer
> In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Lord, I put myself under your protection today. Guard what I wear, what I own, the doors of my house, and everyone who lives here. If anything was stolen or used against me, I place it in your hands. You are stronger than any work done in darkness. Fill this place with your peace. Amen.

### If you think something was done with your belongings
Pray the covering prayer above, wash or discard the item if it troubles you, and stop treating the object as spiritually loaded. In Christian teaching the power is not in the sock; the issue is fear and any open door (occult curiosity, unforgiveness, etc.).

If anxiety stays high, get pastoral help and, if needed, ordinary medical or counseling care. Spiritual seriousness and common sense can sit together.

The broader Afro-Cuban spiritual world includes *trabajos* (ritual works) that some people request or perform against others. These are more commonly associated with mixing traditions or with Palo Mayombe (a related but distinct Congo-derived practice that uses different spirits and tools, including *ngangas*). In popular speech people often lump everything together under “Santería.”

Reported or believed harmful effects include sending *osogbo* (misfortunes) such as:
- Illness or physical decline (*arun*)
- Loss, blocked paths, or financial problems (*ofo*, *ona*)
- Arguments, chaos, or legal trouble (*arayé*, *eyó*)
- Relationship breakdown or isolation
- In extreme folklore or accusations, death or sudden calamity (*iku*, *fitibó*)

These are sometimes called *bilongos* or curses (*epe*). Methods described in ethnographic and practitioner sources typically involve herbs, powders, objects left at a person’s home or workplace, petitions to certain orishas or spirits, or ritual items prepared by a priest.

text:
WHAT YOU POUR INTO YOUR WOMAN IS WHAT YOU RECEIVE IN RETURN.

She is not merely a body you enter.
She is the living chalice, the dark fertile earth, the moon-lit well that receives whatever you offer and returns it multiplied.

Pour presence and she becomes sanctuary.
Pour hunger without reverence and she becomes famine.
Pour your unguarded truth and she becomes the oracle that speaks your own soul back to you.
Pour control and she withholds the waters.
Pour devotion and she opens as the night sky.

The feminine does not invent what she gives you. She alchemizes what you have already placed in her. Your energy is the seed. Her body, her heart, her mystery is the soil. The harvest that appears in your life is simply the same essence wearing a different face.

This is the oldest law of the inner temple: the vessel returns the quality of the wine.

Treat her as sacred and the world around you begins to glow with the same light you gave. Treat her as disposable and you will drink emptiness from every cup that follows.

What you pour is never lost.
It only comes home.

Revelation 17
 
1599 Geneva Bible
17 1 That great whore is described, 2 with whom the Kings of the earth committed fornication. 6 She is drunken with the blood of Saints. 7 The mystery of the woman, and the beast that carried her, expounded. 11 Their destruction. 14 The Lamb’s victory.

1 Then [a]there came one of the seven Angels, which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come: I will show [b]thee the [c]damnation of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters,

2 With whom have committed fornication the kings of the earth, and the inhabitants of the earth are drunken with the wine of her fornication.

3 [d]So he carried me away into the wilderness in the Spirit, and I saw a woman sit upon a [e]scarlet colored beast, full of names of blasphemy, which had seven heads, and ten horns.

4 And [f]the woman was arrayed [g]in purple and scarlet, and gilded with gold, and precious stones, and pearls, [h]and had a cup of gold in her hand full of abomination, and filthiness of her fornication.

5 [i]And in her forehead was a name written, A mystery, [j]that great Babylon that mother of whoredoms, and abominations of the earth.

6 [k]And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of Saints, and with the blood of the Martyrs of JESUS: and when I saw her, [l]I wondered with great marvel.

7 [m]Then the Angel said unto me, Wherefore marvelest thou? I will show thee the mystery of that woman, and of that beast that beareth her, which hath seven heads and ten horns.

8 [n]The beast that thou hast seen, [o]was and is not, and [p]shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and shall go into perdition, and they that dwell on the earth, shall wonder (whose names are not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world) [q]when they behold the beast that was, and is not, and yet is.

9 [r]Here is the mind that hath wisdom, The [s]seven heads [t]are seven mountains, whereon the woman sitteth: [u]they are also seven Kings.

10 [v]Five are fallen, [w]and one is, [x]and another is not yet come: and when he cometh, he must continue a short space.

11 [y]And the beast that was, and is not, is even [z]the eighth, and is [aa]one of the seven, and [ab]all go into destruction.

12 [ac]And the ten horns which thou sawest, are [ad]ten kings, which yet have not received a kingdom, but shall receive power, as Kings [ae]at one hour with the beast.

13 [af]These have one mind, and shall give their power and authority unto the beast.

14 These shall fight with the [ag]Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of Lords, and King of Kings: and they that are on his side, called, and chosen, and faithful.

15 [ah]And he said unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, [ai]are people, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.

16 And the ten [aj]horns which thou sawest upon the beast, are they that shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate, and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.

17 [ak]For God hath put in their hearts to fulfill his will, and to do with one consent for to give their kingdom unto the beast, until the words of God be fulfilled.

18 And that woman which thou sawest, is that [al]great city which reigned over the kings of the earth.

Revelation 17:1 The state of the Church militant being declared, now followeth the state of the Church overcoming and getting victory, as I showed before in the beginning of chapter 10. The state is set forth in 4 chapters. As in the place beforegoing I noted, that in that history the order of time was not always exactly observed, so the same is to be understood in this history, that it is distinguished according to the persons of which it treateth, and that in the several stories of the persons is severly observed in the time thereof. For first is delivered the story of Babylon destroyed, in this and the next chap. (for this Babylon out of all doubt shall perish before the 2 beasts and the Dragon). Secondly is delivered the destruction of both the two beasts, chap. 19. And lastly of the Dragon, chap. 20, in the story of the spiritual Babylon are distinctly set forth the state thereof in this chap. and the overthrow done from God, chap. 18. In this verse and that which followeth is a transition or passage unto the first argument, consisting of a particular calling of the Prophet (as often heretofore) and a general proposition.
Revelation 17:1 That is the damnable harlot, by a figure of speech called hypallage. For S. John as yet had not seen her. Although another interpretation may be borne, yet I like this better.
Revelation 17:1 The sentence that is pronounced against this harlot.
Revelation 17:3 Henceforth is propounded the type of Babylon, and the state thereof in 4 verses. After a declaration of the type, in the rest of this chap., in the type are described two things, the beast (of whom chap. 13), in verse 3, and the woman that sitteth upon the beast, verses 4, 5, 6. The beast in process of time hath gotten somewhat more than was expressed in the former vision. First in that it is not read before that he was appareled in scarlet, a robe imperial and of triumph. Secondly, in that this is full of names of blasphemy: the other carried the name of blasphemy only in his head. So God did teach that this beast is much increased in impiety and injustice and doth in this last age, triumph in both these more insolently and proudly than ever before.
Revelation 17:3 A scarlet color, that is, with a red and purple garment: and surely it was not without cause that the Romish clergy were so much delighted with this color.
Revelation 17:4 That harlot, the spiritual Babylon, which is Rome. She is described by her attire, profession and deeds.
Revelation 17:4 In attire most glorious, triumphant, most rich, and most gorgeous.
Revelation 17:4 In profession, the nourisher of all, in this verse, and teaching her mysteries unto all, verse 5, setting forth all things most magnificently: but indeed most pernicious besotting miserable men with her cup, and bringing upon them a deadly giddiness.
Revelation 17:5 Deceiving with the title of religion, and public inscription of mystery: which the beast in times past did not bear.
Revelation 17:5 An exposition: in which S. John declareth what manner of woman this is.
Revelation 17:6 In manner of deeds: She is red with blood, and sheddeth it most licentiously, and therefore is colored with the blood of the Saints, as on the contrary part. Christ is set forth imbrued with the blood of his enemies; Isa. 3:1.
Revelation 17:6 A passage unto the second part of this chapter, by occasion given of S. John, as the words of the Angel do show, in the next verse.
Revelation 17:7 The second part or place, as I said, verse 1. The narration of the vision, promised in this verse, and delivered in the verse following. Now there is delivered first a narration of the beast and his story, unto verse 14. After, of the harlot, unto the end of the chap.
Revelation 17:8 The story of the beast hath a triple description of him. The first is a distinction of this beast from all that ever hath been at any time: which distinction is contained in this verse: The second is a delineation or painting out of the beast by things present, by which he might even at that time be known of the godly, and this delineation is according to his heads, verses 2, 10, 11. The third is an historical foretelling of things to come, and to be done by him: and these are ascribed unto his horns, verses 12, 13, 14. This beast is that Empire of Rome, of which I spake, chap. 13:11, according to the mutations and changes whereof which then had already happened, the holy Ghost hath distinguished and set out the same. The Apostle distinguisheth this beast from all others in these words. The beast which thou sawest, was and is not. For so I expound the words of the Apostle for evidence’s sake as I will further declare in the notes following.
Revelation 17:8 The meaning is, that beast which thou sawest before (Rev. 13:1) and which yet thou hast now seen, was, (I say was) even from Julius Caesar in respect of beginning, rising up, station, glory, dominion, manner and stock, from the house of Julius: and yet is not now the same, if thou look unto the house and stock for the dominion of this family was translated unto another, after the death of Nero from the other unto a third, from a third unto a fourth, and so forth was varied and altered by innumerable changes. Finally, the Empire is one, as it were one beast: but exceedingly varied by kindreds, families, and persons. It was therefore (saith S. John) in the kindred or house of Julius: and now it is not in that kindred, but translated unto another.
Revelation 17:8 As if he should say, Also the same that is, shall shortly not be: but shall ascend out of the depth, or out of the sea (as was said, Rev. 13:1) that is, shall be a new stock from amongst the nations without difference, and shall in the same state go unto destruction or ruin, and perish: and so shall successively new Princes or Emperors come and go, arise and fall, the body of the beast remaining still, but tossed with so many and often alterations, as no man can but marvel that this beast was able to stand and hold out, in so many mutations. Verily no Empire that ever was tossed with so many changes, and as it were with so many tempests of the sea, ever continued so long.
Revelation 17:8 That is as many as have not learned the providence of God, according to the faith of the Saints, shall marvel at these grievous and often changes when they shall consider, the selfsame beast, which is the Roman Empire, to have been, not to be, and to be and still molested with perpetual mutation, and yet in the same to stand and continue. This in mine opinion is the most simple exposition of this place, and confirmed by the event of the things themselves. Although by the last change also, by which the Empire, that before was civil became Ecclesiastical, is not obscurely signified by these words: of which two, the first exercised cruelty upon the bodies of the saints: the other also upon their souls: the first by human order and policy, the other under the color of the law of God, and of Religion, raged and imbrued itself with the blood of the godly.
Revelation 17:9 An exhortation preparing unto audience, by the same argument, with that of Christ: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. Wherefore, for mine own part, I had rather read in this place, Let there be here a mind, etc. So the Angel passeth fully unto the second place of this description.
Revelation 17:9 Very children know what that seven hilled city is, which is so much spoken of, and whereof Virgil thus reporteth, And compasseth seven towers in one wall: that city it is, which when John wrote these things had rule over the kings of the earth: It was and is not, and yet it remaineth this day, but it is declining to destruction.
Revelation 17:9 This is the painting out of the beast by things present (as I said before) whereby S. John endeavored to describe the same, that he might both be known of the godly in that age, and be further observed and marked of posterity afterwards. This delineation hath one type, that is, his heads, but a double description or application of the type: one permanent from the nature of itself, the other changeable, by the working of men. The description permanent, is by the seven hills, in this verse, the other that fleeteth, is from the seven kings, verses 10, 11. And here it is worthy to be observed, that one type hath sometimes two or more applications, as seemeth good unto the holy Ghost to express either one thing by divers types, or divers things by one type. So I noted before, of the seven spirits, Rev. 1:4. Now this woman that sitteth upon seven hills, is the city of Rome, called in times past of the Greeks, … i. of seven tops or crests, and of Varro, septiceps, i. of her seven heads (as here) of seven heads, and of others, septicollis, i. standing upon seven hills.
Revelation 17:9 The beginning of these Kings or Emperors is almost the same with the beginning of the Church of Christ, which I showed before, Rev. 11:1. Namely from the year 35, after the passion of Christ, what time the Temple and Church of the Jews was overthrown. In which year it came to pass by the providence of God that that saying The beast was and is not, was fulfilled before that the destruction of the Jews immediately following came to pass. That was the year from the building of the city of Rome, 109, from which year S. John both numbered the Emperors which hitherto hath been, when he wrote these things, and foretelleth two others next to come: and that with this purpose, that when this particular prediction of foretelling of things to come, should take effect the truth of all other predictions in the Church might be the more confirmed. Which sign God of old mentioned this in the Law, Deut. 18, and Jeremiah confirmeth, Jer. 28:8.
Revelation 17:10 Whose names are these: the first, Servius Sulpicius Galba, who was the seventh Emperor of the people of Rome, the second Marcus Salvius Otho, the third Aulus Vitellius, the fourth, Titus Flavius Vespasianus, the fifth, Titus Vespasianus his son of his own name.
Revelation 17:10 Flavius Domitian son of the first Vespasian. For in the latter end of his days S. John wrote these things, as witnesseth Irenaus, Lib. 5 adversus hareses.
Revelation 17:10 Nerua. The Empire being now translated from the family of Flavius. This man reigned only one year, four months, and nine days, as the history writers do tell.
Revelation 17:11 This is spoken by the figure synecdoche, as much to say as that head of the beast which was and is not, because it is cut off, and Nerua in so short time extinguished. How many heads there were, so many beasts there seemed to be in one. See the like speech in Rev. 13.3
Revelation 17:11 Nerua Traianus, who himself in divers respects is called here the seventh and the eighth.
Revelation 17:11 Though in number and order of succession he be the eighth, yet he is reckoned together with one of these heads, because Nerua and he were one head. For this man obtained authority together with Nerua, and was Consul with him, when Nerua left his life.
Revelation 17:11 Namely, to molest with persecutions the Churches of Christ, as the histories do accord, and I have briefly noted, Rev. 2:10.
Revelation 17:12 The third place of this description as I said, verse 18, is a prophetical prediction of things to come which the beast should do, as in the words following S. John doth not obscurely signify, saying, which have not yet received the kingdom, etc. For there is an Antithesis or opposition between these kings, and those that went before. And first the persons are described, in this verse, then their deeds in the two verses following.
Revelation 17:12 That is, arising with their kingdoms out of the Roman beast: at such time as that political Empire began by the craft of the Popes greatly to fall.
Revelation 17:12 Namely, with the second beast whom we called before a false prophet, which beast, ascending out of the earth got unto himself all the authority and power of the first beast, and exerciseth the same before his face, as was said, Rev. 14:11, 12. For when the political Empire of the West began to bow downwards, there both arose those ten kings, and the second beast took the opportunity offered to usurp unto himself all the power of the former beast. These kings long ago, many have numbered and described to be ten and a great part of the events plainly testifieth the same in this our age.
Revelation 17:13 That is, by consent and agreement, that they may conspire with the beast, and depend upon his beck. Their story is divided into three parts, counsels, acts, and events. The counselors some of them consist in communicating of judgments and affections: and some in communicating of power, which they are said to have given unto this beast in this verse.
Revelation 17:14 With Christ and his Church, as the reason following doth declare, and here are mentioned the facts and the events which followed for Christ’s sake, and for the grace of God the Father towards those that are called, elected, and are his faithful ones in Christ.
Revelation 17:15 This is the other member of the narration as I said verse 7, belonging unto the harlot, showed in the vision, verse 3. In this history of the harlot, these 3 things are distinctly propounded, what is her magnificence in this verse, what is her fall, and by whom it shall happen unto her, in the two verses following: and lastly, who that harlot is, in the last verse. This place which by order of nature should have been the first, is therefore made the last, because it was more fit to be joined with the next Chap.
Revelation 17:15 That is, as unconstant and variable as the waters. Upon this foundation sitteth this harlot as Queen, a vain person upon that which is vain.
Revelation 17:16 The ten Kings as verse 12. The accomplishment of this fact and event, is daily increased in this our age by the singular providence and most mighty government of God. Wherefore the facts are propounded in this verse, and the cause of them in the verses following.
Revelation 17:17 A reason rendered from the chief efficient cause, which is the providence of God, by which alone S. John by inversion of order affirmeth to have come to pass, both that the Kings should execute upon the harlot, that which pleased God, and which he declared in the verse next beforegoing: and also that by one consent and counsel, they should give their kingdom unto the beast, etc., verses 13, 14. For as these being blinded have before depended upon the beck of the beast that lifteth up the harlot, so it is said that afterward it shall come to pass, that they shall turn back, and shall fall away from her when their hearts shall be turned into better state by the grace and mercy of God.
Revelation 17:18 That is, Rome that great City, or only City (as Justinian calleth it) the King and head whereof was then the Emperor, but now the Pope, since that the condition of the beast was changed.
