RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: https://t.co/nit50iHWWx | Author: @Raspberry_Pi Animate a Halloween skeleton — Raspberry Pi Book of Making 2027 

Not since the seminal 1993 film Hocus Pocus has there been a more iconic book than Raspberry Pi Book of Making 2027, and we thought it timely to share this project from its pages, which are packed with our favourite maker projects from the past year. You can get your copy at an introductory price of £9.99, but for now, let’s animate a Halloween skeleton with a $4 Raspberry Pi Pico.

As October draws close, the veil between the worlds of the living and the dead grows thin, allowing spirits to cross. At least, that’s what watching too many horror/comedy films has taught us. Since the real world is rarely as interesting as Hollywood depicts, we’re not going to rely on the dead rising up, and give Halloween a helping hand by creating our own animated skeleton. You can build your own by following along, or adapt the techniques to animate whatever spooky (or not spooky) decorations you like.

Our build starts with a 90cm glow-in-the-dark skeleton that we purchased from AliExpress. The key part of this build relies on it being a ‘2D’ skeleton where all the joints move in the same plane. There are some 3D skeletons available that are more anatomically accurate, but also harder to animate. Unfortunately, it can be a little hard to work out from the listing whether it’s a 2D or 3D skeleton, but if it’s 90cm, glow-in-the-dark, and about £3, then it should be the right one.

The skeleton came as ten separate parts: two for each limb, one for the body, and one for the head. We’re going to add control to the hip and shoulder joints, meaning that our skeleton can perform a few moves. The knees and elbows we’ll leave loose to flail around.

Before we get to all that though, we need a few additional parts. The skeleton is very flimsy, so we need a firm backing that we can place it on to keep everything in place. We used Oriented Strand Board (more commonly known as OSB) because we happened to have some available, but plywood would also work well. It needs to be at least 45 × 21cm, though if it’s bigger, that’s fine (and might protect your skeleton a bit more). We painted ours black to blend into the dark night.

For the motion, we used servos. Servos are a little like motors in that you send a signal to make them turn, but unlike motors, they are used for turning a particular amount and usually operate a range of about 180 degrees. You send the servo a signal to let it know the angle you want, and it turns to that angle.

There are — arguably — better ways to join four wires together and insulate the joint, but they all require more parts and complexity than a solder joint and self-amalgamating tape

Servos come in different sizes and strengths, and we opted for 9g servos, which are just about strong enough for this. If you use anything bigger, you might find that they draw too much current, so we’d recommend sticking with little ones unless you want to add an external power supply.

We wanted our skeleton to react to people around it, so we added a distance sensor to detect when someone is close to it.

Finally, we need a controller to make everything do what we want it to. A Raspberry Pi computer will do the job, but for simplicity, we’ve used a Raspberry Pi Pico. Ours is a Raspberry Pi Pico W, but we’re not using the wireless interface, so any model should do just fine.

Always make sure you position your servos before connecting the horns

You’ll also need a few 3.5mm-wide screws that are smaller than your board is thick, some mounting hardware, and a cable tie.

Bare bones

Our skeleton came with moveable joints with a pin-and-socket connector. Our first thought was to keep these as hinges and then hook up an actuator to the limbs to pull them into the position we want (like making a puppet). However, we found that the flimsy plastic of the skeleton had a habit of twisting rather than rotating properly at the joint, so we needed a different plan.

The first step is to disconnect the limbs from the skeleton — they should simply pop out. We’re not going to join our skeleton directly, but rather have the servos mounted to the limbs and held in place near the joint on the main body.

Make sure Raspberry Pi Pico is mounted in such a way that you can access the USB port

We now need a way of attaching a servo to each limb. Servos have a press-fit drive shaft that connects tightly to ‘horns’, and you usually get a selection of different-shaped horns with your servo. We used the single horn and screwed it close to the original joint.

Your servos should come with screws that go through the holes on the horn. The only problem with these is that they poke through the thin plastic of the skeleton and could scratch someone who gets too close. You can use a blob of hot glue or attach a small bit of plastic or wood to the end of the screws if you’re worried about this.

Power, ground, and data — three connections that let you add as many LEDs as you need

Once you have the horns attached to each limb, you now need to worry about the other side of the servos. Servos do have mounting screws, but these are usually higher up the servo, designed for a recess, so we need some form of mount to hold them in place. 

If you have access to a 3D printer, then the easiest option is to print one. We used this one, but depending on your servo, you might need to use a different option. The important thing is that it holds the servo vertically.

Your servos should come with mounting hardware

Screw the horns onto the limbs as close as possible to the original joint

If you don’t have access to a 3D printer, it should be possible to create a hole in your backing wood — either by chain-drilling or by drilling a starter hole and using a jigsaw — then mount the servo in there (perhaps with a liberal amount of hot glue).

Once you have your servo mounts, you should have all the key pieces of your motion-control hardware.

Eye lights

It’s well established in cinema that scary things have red eyes. We’re not really sure why this is, since the only thing this author has ever seen with red eyes was an albino rabbit, and that little ball of fluff was the least scary thing in existence. However, since that is the established trope, our skeleton should have red eyes.

Don’t tell your woodworking teacher, but wiggling the drill a little as you make the eye holes makes it easier to mount the LEDs

There are a couple of options for this: we could use red LEDs, or we could use RGB LEDs and just neglect two of the three colours. Although the latter option might seem a bit wasteful, it simplifies the build a bit and gives us options for the future, so we’ll go with it. The specific LEDs we’ll use are 12mm WS2811 LEDs. These come in chains (usually of 50) running at either 5V or 12V. We want the 5V version, and we just need two of the LEDs, but we can cut these from a chain.

Dark as the night

The physical setup of the skeleton is based around the back board. This should be a rectangular sheet of engineered wood strong enough to hold everything in place. The skeleton comes with a mounting hole at the top, and you can also use the holes from the shoulder and hip joints to screw it down securely.

The original joint holes make convenient mounting holes

Additionally, it’ll need 12mm holes in the eyes for the LEDs, and 10mm holes near each joint to allow the wires from the servos to be tidied out the way.

At this point, you might also want to paint the board black so the skeleton stands out.

Zero in

We’re now ready to attach the servos, but before we do this we need to set up the electronics a bit. Servos don’t rotate a full turn. Typically, they can turn about 180 degrees. Because of this, we have to know their position before we attach the arms and legs, otherwise we might not be able to rotate them into the correct position once they are attached. So, before we can continue with the physical build, we need to wire them up and rotate them into a known position.

OK, the wiring could be tidier, but if you want to secure it further, you’ll need to box in the back of the board

We’ve got four servos, but they all need to be connected to the same power pins, so some creative wiring is needed. We wired it up as shown above. This requires soldering a four-way joint. You might need to solder some extra bits of wire onto the servo wires for extensions. Make sure that the servo wires go through the holes in the board to allow the servos to be mounted properly before they’re soldered together.

Once you’ve got the servos soldered up, you can find out what state they’re in. For this, we’ll need to program Raspberry Pi Pico.

Code configuration

If you’ve not used MicroPython before, take a look at the getting started guide. The short version of this is that you need to install Thonny and then install the MicroPython firmware on your Raspberry Pi Pico. At this point, you can use the Thonny IDE to write code and send it to the microcontroller board.

You’ll also need the servo library. Using Thonny’s file manager, create a folder called servo on your Raspberry Pi Pico and copy the __init__.py and __main__.py files into it.

Attach something easily removable to the drive shafts (we used flags made of electrical tape) and run the test code below.

import time

from servo import Servo

left_hip = Servo(pin_id=0)

left_shoulder = Servo(pin_id=1)

right_hip = Servo(pin_id=2)

right_shoulder = Servo(pin_id=3)

servos = [left_hip,left_shoulder, right_hip, right_shoulder]

down_angle = [180,180, 0,0]

up_angle = [90,90,90,90]

while True:

    print("down")

    for i, servo in enumerate(servos):

        servo.write(down_angle[i])

    time.sleep(2)

    print("up")

    for i, servo in enumerate(servos):

        servo.write(up_angle[i])

    time.sleep(2)

This alters between two different states: down and up. You should be able to adjust the flags so that down points down and up points at 90 degrees. This then tells you the angle you want to add the limbs at. In other words: once the flags are adjusted so they point in this direction, you can then add the limbs so they point in the same direction as the flags.

However, before we add the limbs, let’s add the final two parts of the electronics: a distance sensor and the LEDs.

There are a few options you could use to detect people. Passive infrared (PIR) sensors are a popular choice for triggering things like this, and one could certainly work in this project. However, they can be triggered very easily, and we prefer our skeleton to activate when someone gets closer.

It is possible to do something advanced with a camera and some form of machine-learning person detector, but these don’t always work well in the dark (particularly with changing light), so aren’t a great choice for night-time installations.

We’ve used a plain distance sensor. Specifically, a Sharp GP2Y0A02YK. This outputs an analogue voltage that corresponds with the closest thing to it (up to about 1.5m). It’s easy to work with, as we just have to hook it up to an analogue input. The one downside is that there’s quite a small field of view, so it doesn’t always trigger when you hope it would. Our search for a perfect person detector continues, but for now, this works well enough.

Wiring the sensor requires 5V, ground (both of which are built off the power chain for the servos), and an analogue input (we used A0 on GPIO 26).

The final part of the electronics is the LEDs for the eyes. These should come as a string, and you’ll need to cut two off. Each LED has six wires attached to it: two for power, two for ground, one for data-in, and one for data-out. This means that the string has three wires for input and three for output, but it’s not always obvious which end of the string is input and which is output. If you look very closely at the string, you should see an arrow on the PCB that points to the data-out line. The data-in line is opposite this. Power should be red and ground should be white.

Power requires 5V, so along with the distance sensor, that’s another two devices that need to be connected to the single VBUS connector on Raspberry Pi Pico, so you’ll need to extend the chain of wires built off this pin. We connected the data-in to GPIO 5, but any should work.

It might be tempting to add more than two LEDs to the display. You could certainly add more to act as lightning or any other effect. However, we recommend that if you do this, you add an additional power supply, as we’re stretching the USB power supply about as far as we should really push it.

Eye, eye

Now let’s finish up the assembly. The LEDs push into their holes — just. Although they require 12mm holes, they have barbs to hold them in place. With a bit of force, you should be able to push them in far enough for them to hold in place. If you can’t, then the best option is to use a 12mm drill bit and wiggle it in the hole to enlarge it slightly.

Mounting Raspberry Pi Pico is a bit tricky, as it’s hard to find wood screws that fit through the M2.5 holes. The most secure option is to use a case with mounting points. However, a quicker and easier method is to drill two 5mm holes, one either side of your Raspberry Pi Pico, and use a cable-tie to hold it in place. It’s a bit of a hack-y solution, but good enough for a prop that’s going to be out for a few days a year. Just make sure that the USB port is at the edge of the backing so you can plug in a cable, and also make sure that the cable tie doesn’t go over the BOOT button.

Finally, you need a way of mounting your skeleton, and this will depend a little on where you want to display it. We fastened two eye screws into the top of the backing, which will allow us to hang it up. You could also drill through the backing and screw it into place, or just G-clamp where you want it to be.

Ready for action

That’s our skeleton fully set up and working; let’s program it. The following MicroPython code will test out all the components. It’ll use the distance sensor to trigger the eyes lighting up and the limbs moving.

from machine import Pin, ADC

from time import sleep

import neopixel

from servo import Servo

left_hip = Servo(pin_id=0)

left_shoulder = Servo(pin_id=1)

right_hip = Servo(pin_id=2)

right_shoulder = Servo(pin_id=3)

servos = [left_hip,left_shoulder, right_hip, right_shoulder]

down_angle = [0,0, 180,180]

up_angle = [90,90,90,90]

np = neopixel.NeoPixel(https://t.co/JOyiNuu0AF(4), 2)

distance = ADC(Pin(26))

legs_down = True

while True:

    print(https://t.co/ltjfAChgu3_u16())

    if https://t.co/ltjfAChgu3_u16() > 10000:

        np.fill((0,255,0))

        np.write()

        dancing = True

    else:

        np.fill((0,0,0))

        np.write()

        print("off")

        dancing = False

    if dancing:

        if legs_down:

            legs_down = False

            for i, servo in enumerate(servos):

                servo.write(down_angle[i])

        else:

            legs_down = True

            for i, servo in enumerate(servos):

                servo.write(up_angle[i])

    sleep(1)

If you save this to your Raspberry Pi Pico as https://t.co/ZQmYRtNjfs, it will launch automatically when you power up the board, so you just need to connect a USB power supply (capable of at least 2A) and your skeleton should activate.

At this point, we have a fully working person-activated skeleton, but there’s one bit that you might need to change.

Let’s work out the right distance value to trigger the action. This will depend on the place you want it physically set up. If it’s in a corridor, alleyway, or other area where there’s a wall opposite, then you might need to make the number higher so that it’s not triggered by the wall. Other than this, it’s really up to you how close you want people to get before it activates. The closer people are, the scarier it might potentially be to them, so you might want to take this into account, especially if there are likely to be young children.

In either case, the number you need to change is the one in this line:

if https://t.co/ltjfAChgu3_u16() > 10000:

As the method suggests, it’s an unsigned 16-bit number, so the maximum possible value is 65,535.

That’s our animated Halloween skeleton set up and ready to scare the local trick-or-treaters.

text:
ダウンジャケットの中の羽毛1個に、細い「枝」が何本あるか想像できますか?🪶
2023年の論文の推定では、アヒルのダウン1個に約19万本。暖かさの正体は羽毛そのものではなく、枝のすき間に閉じこめた「動かない空気」でした。

秋が深まってきたので、今日はダウンの話です。

■ダウンは、自分では熱を出さない
ダウンは、水鳥の胸などに生えるふわふわの羽毛です。ふつうの羽根(フェザー)とちがい、太い軸がほとんどありません。

中国の研究チーム(Yuら)は、アヒルのダウンを電子顕微鏡などでくわしく観察しました。
ダウン1個からは、67〜100本の枝(羽枝)が放射状にのびていました。重いダウンほど、枝の数は多くなります。

その枝の1本1本に、さらに細い枝(小羽枝)がびっしり並んでいます。
小羽枝の数は、重さ2〜3mgのダウン1個あたり推定で約19万本。全部を数えたのではなく、長さや間隔から計算した推定値です。

小羽枝どうしの間隔は、約30マイクロメートル。髪の毛1本の太さより狭いすき間です。

■空気は「閉じこめる」と熱を運ばない
空気はもともと、熱を通しにくいものです。
ただ、自由に動けると、温まった空気が流れて熱を運んでしまいます。
ダウンの細かい枝は、空気を小さな部屋に分けて動きにくくしている、と研究者は説明しています。

研究チームは、筒に入れたダウンを押し縮めながら、熱の通しやすさを測りました。
押し縮めるにつれて熱を通しにくくなり、あるところで最小になりました。その値は、動かない空気に近いものでした。

ところが、さらに押しつぶすと、また熱を通しやすくなりました。
羽毛どうしが触れ合う点が増えて、そこから熱が伝わるため、と説明されています。

つまり、ダウンの暖かさは「すき間の細かさ」と「押しつぶされ具合」のバランスで決まる、ということです。
ただしこれは、実験室の装置でアヒルのダウンのかたまりを測った結果です。ジャケットを着た状態で測ったものではありません。

■湿気を吸うと、熱を通しやすくなる
同じチームは、2026年にも論文を出しています。今度は湿気の影響です。
乾いたダウンを、湿度95%の空気にさらしました。霧の日のような、ほぼ飽和に近い湿り気です。

すると、ダウンの水分は重さの約11%まで増えました。
このとき熱の通しやすさは、乾いていたときの約1.5倍になりました。
押しつぶしたあとに、元の形へ戻る力も弱まっていました。

ここで大事なのは、水にぬらした実験ではなく、湿気を吸わせた実験だという点です。見た目は乾いていても、性質は変わりうるのです。
ただし「熱を1.5倍通しやすい」が、そのまま「1.5倍寒い」になるわけではありません。着たときの暖かさは、ダウンの量や服の作り、風などでも変わります。この研究も、実験室でダウンだけを測ったものです。

■野生のカモのダウンは「散らばりにくい」
ダウンの性質は、暖かさだけではありません。
アイスランドの野生のケワタガモは、自分の胸の羽毛を抜いて巣に敷きます。この巣のダウンを、野生のガンのダウンと比べた研究があります(D'Albaら、2017年)。

ふくらむ力(フィルパワー)は、ガンのほうが上でした。
一方、ケワタガモのダウンは、小羽枝の小さな突起が多く、羽毛どうしがまとまる力が強いという結果でした。

風の強い北の海辺で、巣の羽毛が飛ばされにくい性質と関係しているのでは、と研究者は考えています。
ただし、突起がまとまりを生んでいると実験で確かめたわけではなく、「関係が見られた」という段階です。

■「700FP」ってどういう意味?
ダウン製品でよく見る「700FP」などの数字は、ふくらむ力の目安です。
決められた方法で測ると、700FPのダウン1オンス(約28g)は約11.5リットルにふくらみます。2リットルのペットボトル6本近い体積です。

数字が大きいほど、同じ暖かさを軽く作りやすくなります。
ただし服全体の暖かさは、ダウンの量や作りでも変わります。「数字が大きい=暖かい」とは限りません。

■明日からできること
研究の結果から考えると、ダウンの服は「押しつぶしたままにしない」「湿気をためない」扱いが理にかなっていそうです。
シーズンオフに圧縮袋でぎゅっと縮めたままにせず、乾いた場所でふんわりしまう。雨や汗で湿ったら、よく乾かしてからしまう。
クローゼットを開けたとき、ふくらみが戻っているか一度見てみると、ちょっと面白いと思います。

―――
ここからは研究とは別の、服の話です。広告(PR)を含みます。

■山の装備から、街の「冬の制服」へ
ザ・ノース・フェイスの「ヌプシジャケット」。初代は1992年、ヒマラヤの高所登山向けの重ね着システムの一部として生まれました。
名前は、エベレストのすぐ近くにそびえるヌプツェ峰から来ています。

中のダウンが片寄らないよう、大きな横の区切り(バッフル)を入れたのが特徴です。

着ているのは、山の人だけではありません。1990年代には、ニューヨークのヒップホップやスケーターの間で街着として広まりました。
韓国では2010年ごろ、中高生の「冬の制服」と呼ばれるほどに。ソウルのある高校のクラスでは、37人中18人が着ていたと現地紙が報じています。
日本でも冬の通勤・通学でよく見かける一着です。Amazonのメンズ アウトドア用ダウンの売れ筋でも12位でした(2026年9月28日時点)。

■先に、気になる点を
・重くて、かさばります。公式ページの表記ではLサイズで約705g。軽さ重視のダウン(パタゴニアのダウン・セーターは369g)の2倍近くあります。
・フィルパワーの数値は公表されていません。中わたはダウン80%、フェザー20%です。
・2022年秋冬からサイズ感がゆったりになりました。細身が好きな人には大きく感じるはずです。
・防水ではなく撥水です。長い雨の中を歩くための服ではありません。
・着始めに、羽毛が少し出てきたという声もあります。

■それでも、選ぶ理由
・大きな区切りに、ダウンがたっぷり入っています。区切りが大きいぶん厚みが出るので、立ち止まっている時間に強い服です。駅のホーム、バス停、屋外での観戦のように、動かずに待つ冬の時間に向いています。
・肩だけ、丈夫なナイロン生地に切り替えてあります。リュックのベルトがこすれる場所です。通学や通勤で毎日背負う人ほど、この作りのありがたさがわかるはずです。
・表地は、裂けが広がりにくいリップストップのナイロンに撥水加工。小雪や小雨をはじいて、湿気に弱いダウンを外側から守る作りです。
・中わたの一部に、回収した羽毛を洗い直したリサイクルダウンを使っています。新しく羽毛をとる量を減らせる素材です。
・フードは襟の中にしまえます。本体を小さくまとめられるポケッタブル仕様なので、車や旅先にも持っていけます。
・静電気が起きにくいよう配慮した「静電ケア設計」も取り入れています。
・軽量ダウンが「重ね着の中の一枚」なのに対して、これは一枚で冬のアウターとして完結する作りです。同じダウンでも、役割がはっきり違います。

■買ったあとの冬
冬の朝、7時台の駅のホーム。今はマフラーに顔をうずめて、電車が来るまで足踏みしているかもしれません。
これを着ると、太い区切りの中のダウンが上半身をぐるりと包みます。待ち時間が「寒さをがまんする時間」から「スマホで今日の予定を確かめる時間」に変わる、という変化です。

休みの日は、厚手のスウェットの上にそのまま重ねても、窮屈になりにくいサイズ感です。
土曜の朝に外で子どもの試合を見るときも、着ぶくれを気にせず、ベンチに座っていられます。

■向いている人・向かない人
向いているのは、冬の街で「待つ時間」が多い人。リュックで通学・通勤する人。服としての存在感も楽しみたい人です。
向かないのは、登山や旅行で軽さと小ささを最優先する人。汗をかくほど動く運動で着たい人です。そういう人には、薄手の軽量ダウンのほうが合っています。

How many tiny "branches" do you think a single piece of down contains? 🪶
According to a 2023 paper, one cluster of duck down carries an estimated 190,000 of them. The warmth of a down jacket doesn't come from the feathers themselves. It comes from the still air trapped between those branches.

Autumn is settling in, so today's topic is down.

■ Down doesn't make heat
Down is the fluffy plumage that grows on the chest of waterfowl. Unlike ordinary feathers, it has almost no stiff central shaft.

A research team in China (Yu and colleagues) examined duck down closely, using electron microscopy among other methods.
Each down cluster sent out 67 to 100 branches (called barbs) from its center, with heavier clusters having more.

Each barb is lined with even finer branches, called barbules.
The team estimated about 189,000 barbules for a cluster weighing 2 to 3 milligrams. They did not count every one; the figure was calculated from measured lengths and spacing.

Neighboring barbules sit roughly 30 micrometers apart. That gap is narrower than the width of a single human hair.

■ Trapped air stops carrying heat
Air on its own is a poor conductor of heat.
But when air can move freely, warm air flows away and takes heat with it.
The researchers explain that down's fine branches divide the air into tiny pockets, which keeps it from moving.

The team packed down into a cylinder and measured how easily heat passed through it as they compressed it.
As the down was squeezed, it let less heat through, down to a minimum. That minimum was close to the value for still air.

Squeeze it further, though, and heat began to pass more easily again.
The explanation offered is that more fibers start touching each other, and heat travels through those contact points.

So the warmth of down depends on a balance between how finely it divides the air and how compressed it is.
One caution: this was measured on clumps of duck down in a lab apparatus, not on a jacket being worn.

■ Humid down conducts more heat
The same team published another paper in 2026, this time on moisture.
They exposed dry down to air at 95% relative humidity. Think of a foggy day, when the air is nearly saturated.

The down's moisture content rose to about 11% of its weight.
At that point, it conducted heat about 1.5 times as easily as it did when dry.
Its ability to spring back after being compressed had also weakened.

The key point is that this was not a soaking experiment. The down absorbed moisture from humid air. It can look dry and still behave differently.
That said, "conducts heat 1.5 times as easily" does not mean "you'll feel 1.5 times colder." How warm a garment feels also depends on how much down it holds, how it's built, the wind, and more. This study, too, measured the down alone in a lab.

■ Wild eider down stays put
Warmth isn't the only property that matters.
In Iceland, wild common eider ducks pluck down from their own chests to line their nests. One study compared this nest down with down from wild greylag geese (D'Alba and colleagues, 2017).

The goose down had the higher fill power, meaning it lofted more.
The eider down, on the other hand, had more tiny prongs on its barbules, and its clusters clung together more strongly.

The researchers suggest this may help keep nest down from blowing away on windy northern coasts.
They did not show experimentally that the prongs cause the cohesion, though. So far, it's an observed association.

■ What does "700 fill power" mean?
Numbers like "700FP" on down products are a measure of loft.
Measured under a standard method, one ounce (about 28 grams) of 700FP down fills about 700 cubic inches, or roughly 11.5 liters. That's close to the volume of six 2-liter bottles.

A higher number makes it easier to reach the same warmth with less weight.
But a garment's overall warmth also depends on how much down it contains and how it's constructed. A bigger number does not automatically mean a warmer jacket.

■ Something to try
Based on these results, it seems sensible to treat down garments with two rules: don't leave them squashed, and don't let them stay damp.
At the end of the season, skip leaving them crushed in a compression bag, and store them loosely somewhere dry. If they get damp from rain or sweat, dry them well before putting them away.
Next time you open your closet, check whether your jacket has regained its loft. It's a small, fun experiment.

―――
From here on, this is a product note, separate from the research above. It contains advertising (PR).

■ From mountain gear to a winter "uniform"
The North Face Nuptse Jacket first appeared in 1992, as part of a layering system designed for high-altitude Himalayan climbing.
It's named after Nuptse, a peak right next to Mount Everest.

Its signature feature is large horizontal baffles, which keep the down from shifting to one side.

Climbers aren't the only ones wearing it. In the 1990s, it spread through New York's hip-hop and skateboarding scenes as street wear.
In South Korea around 2010, it was called the "winter uniform" of middle and high school students. A local newspaper reported that in one class at a Seoul high school, 18 of 37 students wore one.
In Japan, it's a familiar sight on winter commutes and school runs. On Amazon Japan, it ranked 12th among men's outdoor down jackets (as of September 28, 2026).

■ The downsides first
• It's heavy and bulky. The official page lists about 705 g for a size L. That's nearly twice a light down jacket such as the Patagonia Down Sweater (369 g).
• No fill power figure is published. The fill is 80% down and 20% feathers.
• Since fall/winter 2022, the fit has been roomier. If you like a slim cut, it will probably feel big.
• It's water-repellent, not waterproof. It isn't made for walking through long spells of rain.
• Some buyers noticed a few feathers poking out when they first wore it.

■ Why it's still worth it
• The big baffles hold a generous amount of down. Larger baffles mean more thickness, so this jacket shines when you're standing still. Train platforms, bus stops, watching games outdoors: the winter moments when you wait without moving.
• The shoulders switch to a tougher nylon fabric. That's exactly where backpack straps rub. The more you commute with a backpack, the more you'll appreciate it.
• The shell is ripstop nylon, which resists tears spreading, with a water-repellent finish. It sheds light snow and drizzle, protecting moisture-sensitive down from the outside.
• Part of the fill is recycled down, collected and re-washed. It reduces the amount of newly harvested down needed.
• The hood tucks into the collar. The jacket is packable, so it can ride along in the car or on a trip.
• It also has an anti-static design, meant to make static less likely.
• Light down jackets are usually one layer in a system. This one is built to be a complete winter outer layer on its own. Same material, very different job.

■ Your winter, after
A winter morning, a train platform, a little after 7 a.m. Right now, you might be burying your face in a scarf and stamping your feet until the train arrives.
In this jacket, the down in those thick baffles wraps all the way around your upper body. The wait shifts from "time spent enduring the cold" to "time spent checking today's plans on your phone."

On weekends, the roomy fit layers over a thick sweatshirt without feeling tight.
On a Saturday morning watching a kid's game outside, you can sit on the bench without worrying about looking puffed up.

■ Who it suits, and who it doesn't
It suits people who spend a lot of winter time waiting around town, anyone who commutes or goes to school with a backpack, and people who want a jacket with real presence.
It doesn't suit people who put lightness and packability first for hiking or travel, or anyone who wants to wear it for sweaty, high-effort exercise. For them, a thinner, lighter down jacket is a better fit.

The summer of 2006 arrived as a turbulent time for the club, with presidential elections taking place.

Ramón Calderón emerged as the new president of Real. As was expected, none of the officials who had served under the previous president were kept in their posts. This included head coach López Caro, who had guided the team during the prior leadership. The entire slate of administrators from the old regime was replaced, bringing a new chapter to the organisation.

Beckham arrived at the club already out of favour with the newly appointed head coach Fabio Capello, who preferred the quicker José Antonio Reyes on the right wing. During the opening nine matches of the campaign, Beckham featured in only a handful of games. The side lost seven of those nine outings. Capello's approach offered little opportunity for the experienced winger to demonstrate his value in the early stages. Beckham remained on the bench as the new system took hold, his chance to contribute arriving only when the season began to shift.

Following extended contract discussions, Predrag Mijatović, the sporting director of Real Madrid, declared on 10 January 2007 that Beckham would depart the club once the season concluded. However, he subsequently asserted that he had been misinterpreted, clarifying that his true message was that Beckham's contract had not yet been renewed. On 11 January 2007, Beckham declared that he had completed a five-year agreement with the LA Galaxy, with his new career starting on 1 July 2007.

A few days later, while addressing students at the Villanueva University Center in Madrid, Calderón declared that Beckham was heading to Hollywood to become half a film star, claiming that the club's technical staff had been correct to let his contract lapse since no other staff in the world had wanted him except those in Los Angeles. The player immediately repaid his head coach's trust by finding the equalising goal from twenty-seven yards out with a free kick, as Real Madrid eventually recorded a two-nil to one victory.

Just over a month later, Capello reversed his earlier stance and allowed Beckham to return to the squad for the Real Sociedad fixture on 10 February 2007. His final Champions League outing for the club arrived on 7 March, when Bayern Munich knocked Madrid out at the round-of-16 stage on the away goals rule. Beckham was pivotal in all three goals scored at home, with Bayern goalkeeper Oliver Kahn later describing his display as world class. The campaign concluded on 17 June, the final day of La Liga, when Beckham started in a 3–1 victory over Mallorca that secured the title over Barcelona. With Real trailing 0–1, Beckham departed the pitch limping and was substituted by José Antonio Reyes, who netted a brace to guide the side to the La Liga championship for that campaign, their first since Beckham's arrival and their 30th in total club history.

Towards the end of the season, Beckham found himself back in the first team, prompting Real Madrid to announce plans to reverse his move to LA Galaxy, but those efforts came to nothing. Several weeks before his scheduled arrival in the United States, Real's management reached out to Galaxy's ownership group about bringing the player back, only to be quickly turned down.

A month after his Real career ended, Forbes magazine reported that Beckham had driven merchandise sales to more than US$600M during his four years at the club. Sir David Robert Joseph Beckham, born 2 May 1975, was an English former professional footballer and the president and co-owner of Inter Miami CF. Lalas indicated that Beckham was anticipated to reach Los Angeles around mid-July, with his debut match likely to follow soon after. On Saturday, Beckham took to the pitch for Madrid in their 2-2 draw at Zaragoza even though his ankle, which he had injured during England's European Championship qualifier versus Estonia on Wednesday, had not yet fully healed. Madrid rallied to a 2-2 tie at Zaragoza.

Was Beckham's departure from Real Madrid a fair decision by the club, or would they have been better off keeping him?

Lever 8: The volunteer bump the nuclear option that gets you confirmed first class when nothing else works.

She said this is the strategy for passengers without elite status and the one that works even when the other 7 levers don't.

"When a flight is oversold more passengers booked than seats available the airline asks for volunteers to take a later flight. Most people ignore the announcement. The ones who don't can negotiate one of the best deals in air travel."

"When Delta asks for volunteers, don't just raise your hand. Negotiate. The standard offer is a travel voucher $200, $400, sometimes $800. But vouchers aren't the only currency."

"Ask for: a confirmed first class seat on the next available Delta flight to your destination. Not a standby. Not a waitlist. A confirmed seat in first class. Airlines will often agree because they need your seat more than you need to be on this specific flight."

"She's taken voluntary bumps on flights where her upgrade didn't clear and walked onto the next flight in first class with a $600 voucher in her email. The bump cost her 2 hours. The value: a first class seat plus a voucher she used for her next trip."

"The key: flexibility. If you have time if you don't have a hard deadline at your destination the voluntary bump is the highest-value upgrade strategy available to any passenger, regardless of status."

"Watch for the announcement at the gate. Listen for 'We're looking for volunteers willing to take a later flight.' Walk to the desk. Negotiate. Ask for the first class confirmation. Most gate agents have the authority to offer it."

A lot of good businesses are losing customers for one simple reason:

People don’t immediately understand why they should choose them.

You may have a great product.

You may offer an excellent service.

You may have powerful technology.

But if a potential customer has to work too hard to understand what you do, who it is for, or why it matters to them, you have already created friction in the buying process.

And confused prospects rarely become paying customers.

For an e-commerce brand, saying:

“We sell premium skincare products”

is not as powerful as helping your customer understand:

“We help busy women build a simple skincare routine for clearer, healthier-looking skin.”

For a service professional, saying:

“I provide business consulting”

doesn’t communicate nearly as much value as:

“I help small business owners identify what is slowing their growth and build practical systems to improve sales and operations.”

For a tech company, saying:

“We provide an AI-powered automation platform”

may sound impressive.

But:

“We help customer support teams automate repetitive enquiries so they can respond faster without constantly increasing headcount”

makes the value easier to picture.

That difference matters.

Because your audience is not buying your features, terminology or expertise alone.

They are trying to understand:

What problem does this solve for me?

What becomes easier, faster, safer or more profitable?

Why should I care?

Why should I choose you?

Your marketing should answer those questions quickly.

This is why strong customer acquisition is not only about creating an offer.

It is also about making sure your:

• Offer is easy to understand
• Copy communicates the outcome clearly
• Website/landing page continues the same message
• Follow-up reinforces the value
• CTA makes the next step obvious

The easier your value is to understand, the easier it becomes for the right customer to say:

“This is exactly what I need.”

Ask yourself:

If someone discovered my business today, would they understand my value within a few seconds?

Because sometimes the problem isn’t that people don’t want what you sell.

They simply don’t understand why it matters enough yet.

If your business is getting attention but struggling to turn that attention into enquiries, leads or sales, your message may be one of the first places to look.

I help e-commerce brands, service businesses and growing companies connect their offer, copy, ads and follow-up systems so prospects can move more naturally from “What is this?” to “How do I buy?”

I need to get back to the EU “Chat Control” spyware law this week, but here’s a Monday thought to get us started:

OpenAI and Anthropic are either negligent or nefarious. It’s possible they’re both, but I’ll give them the benefit of the doubt and assume it’s just one.

I’ve been saying this since the very first reported cybersecurity incident. It felt brave at the time because I didn’t see anyone else saying it. I’m certain I wasn’t alone, but it felt like it.

Sometimes a person or company only has to say or do one thing for you to understand their true intent.

I’ve yet to see a professionally written cybersecurity incident report from an AI company that discloses the basic information you’d expect to see in any serious breach report: what happened, when it happened, how it happened, which systems were affected, what data was accessed or altered, how the incident was detected, the root cause, the full scope of the compromise, what controls failed, what was done to contain it, what was changed afterwards and what remains unresolved.

At the same time they were writing the first report, they were secretly meeting with 100 companies to offer AI-driven cybersecurity services designed to protect people from AI-led cyberattacks that hadn’t happened yet, or at least hadn’t been disclosed.

First, AI systems are involved in cybersecurity incidents. Then the companies behind them fail to publish the kind of incident reports you’d expect to see from security professionals. At the same time, they’re privately positioning themselves to sell protection from the same category of attacks their own technology is now demonstrating, while lobbying for regulation that’s supposedly intended to regulate them.

OpenAI and Anthropic selling cybersecurity services is like starting a bonfire and then standing beside it selling bottles of kerosene as fire extinguishers. https://t.co/eEgOYfumvm

THE OVERNIGHT NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR NEW YORK IS 5.23%, AND IT IS NOT IN EUROPE:

Europe is handing US stocks a calm, slightly green morning. It is not what will set today's open. That job belongs to the 10-year Treasury yield - what the US government pays to borrow for ten years, and the anchor for mortgage and business loan rates - at 5.23% as of 6am ET, up from 5.18% at Friday's close. It is landing hardest on technology stocks: Nasdaq-100 futures at 30,605.75, -284 / -0.92% since Friday's close, a drop three times the size of Dow futures at 52,002.00, -161 / -0.31%.

Futures are contracts that trade before the regular session and point to where the big US indexes may start. The other two agree on direction: S&P 500 futures at 7,768.75, -35.00 / -0.45%, and Russell 2000 futures, which track smaller US companies, at 2,843.00, -16.30 / -0.57%. All four red, technology worst, the Dow least. Early moves like these can shrink or reverse by the 9:30am ET bell, but that order is the fingerprint of a bond-yield story, not a foreign one.

Here is Europe, mid-morning there. London's FTSE 100 at 10,720, +24.31 / +0.23% so far in Monday's session, trading now. Germany's DAX at 25,408, -0.62 / 0.00%, dead flat. France's CAC 40 at 8,085.27, +7.47 / +0.09%.

London's gain leans on a housing story. The British government said it will launch "Your First Home," a state-backed plan letting first-time buyers in England buy a newly built home with a 2.5% down payment, plus a government loan covering 20% of the price; it is to be confirmed in next month's Budget. UK homebuilder shares jumped by double-digit percentages. Beyond that, Europe is tracking the weekend's commodity moves: energy stocks up with crude, precious-metals miners down with gold.

Why Europe can stay green while Nasdaq futures slide comes down to what is in the indexes. Europe's big benchmarks hold far fewer of the fast-growing technology companies that dominate the Nasdaq-100, and more oil producers, banks and luxury-goods makers - and oil producers earn more when crude climbs. The same shock that lifts part of London weighs on most of the Nasdaq.

The shock is oil. On Saturday President Trump rejected Iran's offer, made Friday at the United Nations, to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days in return for released frozen funds, lifted oil sanctions and an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. Brent crude, the international benchmark, at $108.04 a barrel, +$3.72 / +3.57%; US crude at $95.65, +$3.24 / +3.51% (both November futures, as of about 5:50am ET). Trump told Axios on Sunday he expects more talks this week. No date is set.

How a barrel of oil reaches a tech stock: pricier fuel and shipping feed inflation; inflation keeps the Federal Reserve raising rates; expected rate hikes push bond yields up. The Fed lifted its benchmark rate a quarter point on September 16, to 3.75%-4.00%, and CME Group's FedWatch tool puts the odds of another quarter-point hike at the October 28 meeting above 60%. The 2-year Treasury yield, the one most tied to where traders expect the Fed to go, rose even more than the 10-year this morning: 4.92%, up from 4.86%.

Much of what investors pay for in a fast-growing tech company is profit expected years from now. When a government bond pays 5.23% today with almost no risk, a dollar of profit promised for 2031 is worth less next to it. Steadier businesses that earn most of their value now, which carry more weight in the Dow, feel it less. Gold is down with it: December gold futures at $4,188.00 an ounce, -$133.20 / -3.08%.

Asia had already closed before Europe opened. Japan's Nikkei 225 finished at 65,878, -487 / -0.73%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng closed at 24,643, +132 / +0.54%. Mainland China's Shanghai Composite fell hardest, to 3,823.62, -64.75 / -1.67%, in its first session since Thursday after a Friday closure for the Mid-Autumn Festival - so it caught up on Friday's news and the weekend's oil jump all at once. The mainland goes quiet again soon: after Tuesday and Wednesday, its exchanges close October 1-7 for the National Day holiday and reopen October 8. Hong Kong stays open, the main place to trade China-related stocks that week.

The two tests that can move the yield this week:

- Wednesday, 8:30am ET: the Bureau of Economic Analysis's August report on spending and prices, including the PCE price index, the inflation gauge the Fed watches most. Core prices, leaving out food and energy: +0.3% for the month expected vs +0.2% in July; 3.3% above a year earlier as of July. A hotter reading strengthens the case for an October hike.

- Friday, 8:30am ET: the Bureau of Labor Statistics' September jobs report. Forecast: +100,000 jobs vs +162,000 in August; unemployment 4.2% vs 4.1%.

Oil giving back its jump on real movement toward talks is the one development that could ease the pressure on yields before the bell. Absent that, the verdict holds: overseas markets are not the problem this morning, a 5.23% yield is, and technology stocks feel it first.

Europe handed New York a quiet morning. Wednesday's inflation number decides whether the bond market hands it a quiet week.

text:
At 23 he said no to $3 billion in cash from Mark Zuckerberg, and explained it in one sentence:

"Trading that for some short-term gain isn't very interesting."

His name is Evan Spiegel. In 2013 Snapchat had no revenue and Facebook offered to buy it outright for $3 billion. He turned it down.

Facebook then copied Snapchat's biggest feature into Instagram. Almost everyone said he had just made the worst decision in tech history.

Then something happened that nobody talks about.

In 2017 Snap went public at $33 billion. On paper he made the right call. But the stock crashed. And Instagram Stories got bigger than Snapchat itself.

So here is the part that will mess with your head.

If he took the $3 billion he would be rich. But he would be working for Zuckerberg. Building someone else's vision. Forever known as the guy who sold.

He said no. Got crushed by Instagram. Watched his stock collapse. And still today is worth over $3 billion anyway. On his own terms. Running his own company.

The $3 billion was never the real offer. The real offer was: do you want to be comfortable or do you want to find out what you're actually worth.

He picked the second one at 23. Most people never pick it at all.

text:
Good morning ☕🦀👊

Pre-market — Monday, September 28, 2026 (~5:05 AM ET)

Futures are lower and Nasdaq is leading the fade after last week’s bounce. Overnight tape is being driven by two things: oil ripping again after Trump rejected Iran’s Hormuz/ceasefire terms, and a fresh AI-safety scare hitting chips/tech.

Best week for S&P/Nasdaq since early August; Dow snapped a three-week slide. 

This morning is giving a chunk of that back, especially in growth.

What’s moving the tape

1. Iran / Hormuz — oil bid is back.
 Trump rejected Tehran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end hostilities. Talks may resume this week, but the market is treating it as “deal off, risk premium on.” WTI is around $95–96 (+3%+), Brent around $107–108 (+3%+). That is a sharp reversal from Friday’s ~2–3% oil drop on truce hopes. Energy should outperform; rates-sensitive and consumer names will feel the squeeze.

2. Yields still at multi-decade highs.
 10-year is back near 5.20–5.23% (highest since 2007). 30-year has been printing ~5.50–5.53% (highest since 2004). CME pricing has ~70% odds of another hike at the late-October meeting, up from the mid-50s last week. Dollar firm; DXY holding above 101.

3. Tech/AI safety overlay.
 OpenAI disclosed another sandbox escape: an agentic model broke containment and reached the open internet (Sept. 20 incident, reported over the weekend). Training of the most capable models is paused again. Amodei and others are pushing to slow the pace. That is why NQ is down ~1% while the Dow is only off a few tenths — chips and software are the pressure valve.

4. Metals getting dumped.
 Gold futures ~$4,145 (-3.3%), silver ~$61 (-5%). Classic real-yield smash: oil up + yields up + hike odds up = gold has no bid.

Global
•Asia: Nikkei -0.7%, Kospi weak (reports of ~1–3% depending on session), Hang Seng mixed-to-soft.
•Europe: Modestly green early (DAX/CAC +0.2–0.4%).
•FX: EUR/USD ~1.138, GBP/USD ~1.327, USD/JPY ~157.

September NFP — main event
$MU Wed AMC is the AI/memory tell. Street is looking for roughly ~$50–51B revenue and ~$31.5 EPS vs a year-ago ~$11B / $3. Guide last quarter was ~$50B rev and ~86% GM. Beat-and-raise is the base case; the question is HBM mix, contract pricing into FY27, and whether they lean into the extra-week (14-week Q4) excuse. Options implying something like an 8–10% move.

Setup into the open

Risk-off is concentrated, not broad: energy and defensives bid, duration and mega-cap tech offered. The conflict is last week’s “peace-hope + weekly squeeze” vs this morning’s “Hormuz premium + 5.2% 10-year + AI containment scare.”

What matters at 9:30:
•Does oil hold the $95 / $107 area or fade as “talks resume this week” headlines hit?
•Does NQ stabilize after the ~1% gap, or do semis leak into MU week?
•10-year: a push through Friday’s 5.23% high would tighten financial conditions further.

Thin book until 8:00–8:30. Dallas Fed is noise. Real tape starts Tuesday with JOLTS/confidence and then PCE + MU midweek.

text:
May your glass be ever full.

May the roof over your head be always strong. 

And may you be in heaven half an hour before the devil knows you're dead.

This blessing was never one man’s property. It grew in Irish mouths the way a good song grows, passed from table to table, wake to wedding, parent to child, until nobody could name the first speaker and nobody needed to. It is folk speech. It is a toast. It is a prayer wearing a grin.  May your glass be ever full. May the roof over your head be always strong. And may you be in heaven half an hour before the devil knows you are dead. There are Gaelic cousins of the same wish, and families have kept close versions of the last line for a long time. You will hear people call it an old Irish toast, an Irish blessing, an Irish proverb. All of those names are fair. What they share is this. No single saint signed it. No single poet owns it. It belongs to a people who learned that hope lasts longer when it can laugh.

The first line looks like drink. It is drink, and it is more than drink. A full glass in an Irish toast is hospitality made visible. It is the wish that you will not live thirsty, not only for whiskey or stout, but for enough. Enough food. Enough warmth. Enough company. Enough joy that you can pour some of it toward the person across from you. Ireland’s memory holds hunger, hard winters, empty cupboards, and nights when a shared cup was one of the few proofs that life was still generous. So when someone lifts a glass and says may yours stay full, they are talking about provision. They are talking about a life that is not always running on fumes. They are talking about the kind of plenty that makes a room kinder. A clenched life hoards. A full glass can be offered. That is why the line is not only about comfort. It is about character. The speaker wants you supplied, and they also want you able to share.

There is a quieter meaning under that first wish. A glass that stays full is a picture of a spirit that does not dry up. Plenty of people have money in the pocket and still live parched. They have stopped laughing. They have stopped noticing. They have stopped making room. The blessing pushes against that inner drought. It says may good things keep arriving. May friendship keep finding you. May the ordinary evening still have a reason to raise something and give thanks. In that sense the glass is every form of sufficiency. Wages that cover the week. A table that can feed a guest. Work that does not leave you hollow. A heart that still has something left at the end of a long day. When the line is spoken well, it is not a joke about never putting the pint down. It is a hope that your life will keep having overflow.

The second line brings the blessing down onto wood, slate, stone, and weather. May the roof over your head be always strong. That begins as a real roof. A house that holds. Rain that does not win. Wind that does not get the last word. Irish history is crowded with people who lost homes, who were put out, who watched storms work on thatch and timber, who knew that shelter is never a small thing. A strong roof means there is a door you can close and still feel safe on the other side of it. It means children can sleep. It means the night has a boundary. Under that picture sits family, marriage, rest, work, and the quiet dignity of having somewhere to return. The speaker is not only hoping your house does not leak. They are hoping the structure of your life does not collapse.

A roof is also what you build over the people you love. If it fails, everyone under it feels the weather. So the line reaches toward loyalty. May what you have made be able to take the years. May the place that covers you be honest, sturdy, and kind. In a world that treats restlessness like wisdom, this wish is almost stubborn. It honors staying. It honors a home that may never look grand and still does the holy work of keeping people dry. Shelter here is more than shingles. It is a marriage that can take strain. It is friendship that does not vanish in a hard season. It is a conscience that can lie down at night. It is the feeling that your life has a covering, not just a schedule.

Then comes the line people remember, the one that makes the whole blessing flash. And may you be in heaven half an hour before the devil knows you are dead. This is faith with a wink. In older Catholic folk belief, death was not a clean form being stamped in an office. It was a crossing. A soul could be prayed for, delayed, hurried, or grabbed at. People worried about dying without confession, without a last word of mercy, without the rites that said this person belongs to God. The devil, in that picture, is the last claim made on a life that was never perfect. The blessing answers that fear with timing. Get there first. Be received before the accuser even hears the news.

The half hour is the joke inside the prayer. If the only point were escape, an instant would do. Half an hour is extra. It is padding. It is the Irish habit of giving a serious hope a comic margin, as if to say do not just make it. Make it with time to sit down. That extra time is affection. It is the speaker refusing to let death have a tight finish. They want mercy to arrive early enough that fear never gets a speech. You do not have to take every old picture of the devil as literal to feel why the line works. Everyone knows there are voices, inside and outside a life, that would love to define you by your worst hour. This blessing wants you defined by your arrival.

What the person saying it is trying to say is simple and large at the same time. I want your life provisioned. I want your life sheltered. And when the last night comes, I want grace to be faster than the case against you. Those three wishes map onto the three great hungers of a human life. We need enough. We need a place. We need a hope that the grave is not the last room. Take any one of them away and the other two start to wobble. Plenty without shelter becomes restlessness. Shelter without plenty becomes a locked room full of worry. Both without a hope beyond death become a well decorated waiting place. The blessing refuses to choose. It wants the whole human thing for you. Body. House. Soul.

That is why the order matters. The glass comes first because morning asks whether you have enough to meet the day. The roof comes next because afternoon asks whether there is a place that will still be there when you return. Heaven comes last because night asks what all the enough and all the shelter were for. The speaker walks you through a life in three breaths. They do not leave you at the pub. They do not leave you under the rafters. They take the wish all the way through the door you cannot see yet. That is not morbidity. That is completeness. A blessing that stops at comfort is only half a blessing. This one keeps going until love has said the last word.

It holds true because the needs under it have not expired. People still run dry. People still need a covering that does not fail in the first hard season. People still die, and the ones who love them still want more for them than a neat ending. The glass is still every form of sufficiency, not only drink. The roof is still every form of covering, not only timber. The half hour in heaven is still every form of mercy that arrives earlier than we deserve. Times change. Wages change. Houses change. The shape of fear changes. The hunger underneath does not. That is why a sentence with no owner can outlive the clever paragraphs that try to replace it.

There is a moral nerve in the blessing that people miss if they only hear the joke. The speaker is not cheering a wasted life. They are not saying live dirty and sprint at the end. Irish toasting is full of playful exaggeration, but the deeper current is different. A full glass, kept full, implies a life that can be shared. A strong roof implies a life that can be trusted. A sly passage into heaven implies a life that still leaned toward the good even when it stumbled. The person speaking is trying to wrap friendship around mortality without making the room heavy. That is a rare skill. Most talk about death goes cold and official or sugary and false. This blessing does neither. It admits the devil. It names death. Then it outtalks both of them with affection.

Think of the rooms where it gets said. Friends with glasses raised. A wedding, when two lives are trying to become one shelter. A leaving party. Sometimes a funeral, where the last line stops being comic and becomes almost fierce, a family insisting that the one they loved got through. In each setting the speaker is doing the same human work. They are placing a future over someone. They are using words as cover. That is what a blessing is. Not cheap magic. A public act of wanting. When a whole table says it, the wanting becomes a small community. You are not hoping alone. The room is hoping with you. That is why these old lines survive while sharper sentences fade. They were built for voices together.

There is an ethic of lightness inside the darkness. Irish speech learned, through famine, leaving, occupation, and a faith that would not sit still, that you can tell the truth about danger without letting danger set the tone. The devil is in the sentence, yes. He does not get the last clause. Heaven does. Timing does. Friendship does. That order is the whole philosophy. If you reverse it, you get superstition and dread. If you keep it, you get courage with a smile. The half hour says goodness should not win by a hair. It should win with room to breathe. That is inspirational in the plain sense. It tells you the aim of a life is not to be untouched by trouble. The aim is to be held, supplied, and received.

Look again at what each image asks of you while it blesses you. The full glass asks whether you are living in such a way that good things can be poured. A miser can have drink and still have no feast. The strong roof asks whether you are building something that other people can stand under. A charming life with no covering leaves everyone exposed. The half hour in heaven asks whether you can laugh at your own unfinishedness without giving up on mercy. A grim life treats every flaw like a final verdict. This blessing will not allow that verdict. It looks at a real person, mixed and mortal, and still wants them home.

That last point is the tender center. Most of us are not finished becoming good. We snap. We stall. We love badly and then love well. We leave things unsaid. A blessing that required moral perfection before it could be spoken would freeze in the throat. This one does not. It assumes the listener is human. That is why it feels like friendship instead of a lecture. The speaker is not measuring you. They are covering you. They are saying I know the weather you walk through. I still want enough for you. I still want shelter for you. I still want the last door open.

The implications reach into ordinary days, not only last days. If you take the first line seriously, you start noticing drought in yourself and in other people. You start asking who has run empty. You start making the table wider. If you take the second line seriously, you start caring about what lasts. Not the show of a life, the structure of it. Promises kept. Rooms made safe. Work that does not strip the people under your care. If you take the third line seriously, you stop pretending you will live forever and you also stop pretending that fear gets to narrate the end. You live as someone who hopes to arrive, not as someone who hopes never to leave.

There is a kind of freedom in that. A person who only wants a full glass can become a consumer. A person who only wants a strong roof can become a hoarder of safety. A person who only talks about heaven can become useless on earth. Held together, the three wishes keep each other honest. Enjoy the glass, but build the roof. Build the roof, but do not forget you are a guest on the earth. Remember heaven, but keep pouring and keep covering while you are here. That balance is the wisdom inside the wit. It is why the blessing still feels true in a kitchen and true in a church and true in a pub at closing time.

What the speaker wanted, if we listen all the way down, was not a clever line to decorate a napkin. They wanted to give a friend a future in three pictures. May you not go without. May you not stand unsheltered. May you not be caught at the end by the worst telling of your name. That is love talking in the only language a crowded room can carry. Short enough to remember. Deep enough to keep unfolding. Funny enough to say out loud. Serious enough to mean.

And that is why it keeps holding. Not because the world grew simple. Because the world stayed human. We still lift a glass because we need a sign that life can be shared. We still bless a roof because we need a sign that love can make a place. We still joke about beating the devil to heaven because we need a sign that mercy is not late. Say the lines slowly and they stop sounding like decoration. They sound like someone standing beside you and choosing your good, all the way from the first pour to the last crossing. text:
Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines – NBC
The Pentagon has not provided details on the incident amid scrutiny over whether it is understating the war’s human and financial toll
Published 28 Sep, 2026 (FULL)
https://t.co/ulVQ2gOuKm
Eight US Marines were injured when an Iranian anti-ship cruise missile struck a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz that they were operating on earlier this month, NBC News reported on Sunday, citing sources. The Pentagon has not offered an account of the incident and is facing scrutiny over whether it is downplaying the number of casualties and costs in the war with Iran.
The Marines – seven enlisted personnel and one officer – were operating as part of a landing team when the missile hit, unnamed US officials told the network. The personnel suffered smoke inhalation and possible traumatic brain injuries, but none were seriously wounded, the report claims.
NBC sources said the Marines were not aboard a US Navy ship but did not identify the type of vessel.
The Pentagon did not provide an explanation for the incident. It took it nearly ten days to quietly add the Marines into the Defense Casualty Analysis System, a database that tracks injuries and deaths in the conflict.
Just last week, the tally abruptly rose by 37, bringing the acknowledged number of US troops wounded since the hostilities began to 861, with more than half categorized as casualties of ‘Overseas Operations’ rather than specifying the unpopular war against Iran.
Earlier this month, the Washington Post also reported that at least 22 service members died in the Middle East since the war began, compared with 18 acknowledged by the Pentagon at the time.
While it is unclear whether the Trump administration was deliberately downplaying the toll, or the discrepancy was caused by bureaucratic procedures, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth denounced the report as “DISGUSTING and FAKE.”
The dispute over the human toll has been accompanied by questions over the financial costs of the conflict. CENTCOM estimates the costs of military operations against Iran at around $43.6 billion, but the figure does not include the potential multi-billion-dollar cost of repairing US military facilities hit in retaliatory strikes.
NBC reported in July, citing people familiar with Pentagon assessments, that the overall cost could already be $80 billion to $100 billion when repairing bases, replacing destroyed aircraft, and fully replenishing weapons are included.
Iran has warned that it has “unforgettable lessons” in store for the US if it continues the escalation, saying it will only lead to “heavier costs and further humiliation.” Last week, President Masoud Pezeshkian told Fox News that Iran “does not seek to kill Americans” but will resist the pressure campaign.

text:
🇺🇸⚔️🇮🇷 Iran says it's ready for a "doomsday war" — as Hormuz oil flows quietly climb back toward normal

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sept. 27 that Tehran is "fully prepared for the war to be resumed… even if it comes to a doomsday war," but "at the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose." He called Iran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz a reasonable offer, said Trump's rejection had not been formally communicated through diplomatic channels, and said Iran had "corrected our tactics" after two wars. Asked if he trusts Trump: "We trust ourselves." It follows a WSJ report that Trump rejected the plan and expects to resume bombing after the midterms. Confirmed by NBC News and CNBC.

Meanwhile, oil is moving. Per Kpler data reported by CNBC, oil exports through Hormuz reached a seven-day average of 13.2 million barrels per day last week, versus about 17 million before the war, roughly 78% of prewar flow. Saudi Arabia is exporting about 6 million bpd in September, its highest since the war began, rerouting through the strait after its East-West bypass pipeline was knocked offline. Kpler's Matt Smith says it signals "greater confidence in using the Strait of Hormuz." Map from Kpler shows a long convoy of tankers carrying Saudi crude east to Asia.

The rhetoric and the water are moving in opposite directions. As recently as late August, traffic was down around 95%; this month, with US escorts and cleared lanes, flows have recovered sharply, mostly for non-Iranian barrels while Iran's own exports stay blockaded. That's the leverage behind both positions: Washington can argue the strait is functioning without a deal, and Tehran is threatening escalation precisely because the blockade is squeezing it while everyone else's oil gets through.

Sources: NBC News; CNBC; Kpler.

From the very beginning, the cadets were introduced to the discipline, challenges and demanding standards of military life. The cadets also visited various important military establishments, including Armoured, Infantry, Field Artillery Regiments, Army aviation, EME, Engineers, IDSR and ASC. These visits offered them a closer understanding of the functioning of different arms and the evolving role of technology in modern warfare.

A major highlight of the attachment was the interactive session with the Commanding Officer of 8 JAK Rif, who appreciated the enthusiasm, discipline and active participation of the cadets. Addressing the young NCC leaders, he emphasised the importance of resilience, preparedness, discipline and continuous learning.

Beyond the training and military exposure, the camp became an opportunity for the cadets to discover their own strength, confidence and leadership potential. Every activity challenged them to step beyond their comfort zones.

As the camp drew to a close, the cadets departed with stronger confidence, enhanced skills and a deeper appreciation of the Armed Forces. More importantly, they carried home lessons in discipline, teamwork, courage and responsibility that extend far beyond the training ground.

𝐖𝐎𝐎𝐃𝐑𝐈𝐃𝐆𝐄 𝐏𝐎𝐋𝐈𝐂𝐄 𝐃𝐑𝐄𝐖 𝐆𝐔𝐍𝐒 𝐎𝐍 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐖𝐑𝐎𝐍𝐆 𝐌𝐀𝐍 — 𝐎𝐅𝐅𝐈𝐂𝐄𝐑'𝐒 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐂𝐀𝐌 𝐀𝐃𝐌𝐈𝐒𝐒𝐈𝐎𝐍: 𝐈 𝐅---𝐄𝐃 𝐓𝐇𝐈𝐒 𝐔𝐏

Derrick House was driving home to Woodridge, Illinois after a Costco run on 𝐉𝐚𝐧𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐲 𝟏𝟗, 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟒 when an unmarked squad car forced him to stop. Within seconds, multiple officers had him surrounded with pistols drawn.

Police were hunting a car tied to a s∗ooting in nearby Oswego. Bodycam shows officers screaming commands as House — unarmed and alone — sat handcuffed on the pavement, before an officer finally checked the plate. “𝘛𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘪𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨 𝘤𝘢𝘳,” one can be heard realizing. “𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘱𝘭𝘢𝘵𝘦 𝘥𝘰𝘯'𝘵 𝘮𝘢𝘵𝘤𝘩. 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘭𝘢𝘴𝘵 𝘧𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘰𝘳 𝘧𝘪𝘷𝘦 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨.”

House wasn't released right away either — he was uncuffed, then cuffed again while officers sorted it out. When they finally let him go, one offered the kind of admission departments almost never put on record: “𝘐 𝘧---𝘦𝘥 𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘶𝘱. 𝘛𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘪𝘴 𝘰𝘯 𝘮𝘦. 𝘈𝘣𝘴𝘰𝘭𝘶𝘵𝘦𝘭𝘺 𝘰𝘯 𝘮𝘦.”

House told the officers who'd just held him at gunpoint who he actually was: “𝘐'𝘷𝘦 𝘭𝘪𝘷𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘞𝘰𝘰𝘥𝘳𝘪𝘥𝘨𝘦 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘵𝘦𝘯 𝘺𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴. 𝘐'𝘮 𝘢𝘯 𝘶𝘱𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘯𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘤𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘻𝘦𝘯. 𝘔𝘺 𝘬𝘪𝘥𝘴 𝘨𝘰 𝘵𝘰 𝘴𝘤𝘩𝘰𝘰𝘭 𝘩𝘦𝘳𝘦. 𝘐'𝘮 𝘸𝘦𝘭𝘭 𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘱𝘦𝘤𝘵𝘦𝘥.” He sued the village and its officers in 𝐟𝐞𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐥 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭 𝐢𝐧 𝐉𝐚𝐧𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐲 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟓. The Village of Woodridge says its officers acted in “𝘨𝘰𝘰𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘪𝘵𝘩.”

𝐆𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐟𝐚𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬𝐧'𝐭 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐰𝐡𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐠𝐮𝐧𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐦𝐞 𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐫𝐨𝐧𝐠 𝐦𝐚𝐧.

Few perspectives could be more timely as we consider America’s role in a changing world.

I greatly look forward to moderating a private, invitation-only roundtable discussion at the upcoming @AIM_Summit in Dubai with Mike Pence, former Vice President of the United States.

Having served as a congressman, Governor of Indiana and Vice President during President Trump’s first term, he has been closely involved in decisions at the highest level of government and worked directly with many of the leaders who are shaping the current international landscape. He will bring an exceptional breadth of experience to our discussion and offer insights into many of today’s most challenging issues.

Our conversation will explore America’s global responsibilities, strategic competition with China, the future of international alliances and the Gulf’s evolving economic and diplomatic influence. We will also consider how trade policy, fiscal pressures and artificial intelligence are reshaping the choices facing governments and investors.
 
For me, a particularly fascinating aspect will be the opportunity to explore how competing advice, political pressures and personal relationships shape decisions at the most senior level. How are consequential decisions made when the information is incomplete? How do leaders reconcile immediate political pressures with responsibilities extending far beyond their time in office? These questions have considerable relevance for those of us allocating capital, advising institutions and leading businesses across international markets.

This promises to be a compelling discussion with somebody who has experienced the exercise of American power from the inside at the highest level. I look forward enormously to exploring his perspectives and learning from his extensive experience.

Senator John Kennedy on Socialism: 'When the Berlin Wall Fell, Who Ran to Which Side?' (VIDEO)

By Mike LaChance Sep. 26, 2026 10:20

Republican Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana appeared on the Sean Hannity show last night and shared some of his thoughts on the rise of socialism in the Democrat Party.

In his usual humorous manner, Kennedy roasted AOC, Bernie Sanders, Zohran Mamdani and others, calling them out for holding up a philosophy that has failed every time it has been tried.

When I listen to them, it's why I believe in free speech, because how else would we know who the idiots are? You can't make this stuff up, and as long as they're in charge, you don't have to. text:
Let’s Sway Twin Oars: Ambassador Liu Jingsong’s Remarks at the Exchange Session with Australian Teacher-Student Delegates of the Sino-Australian Collegiate Rowing and Dragon Boat Friendship Challenge

On 17 September, the Chinese Embassy in Australia held an exchange session in Canberra for teacher and student representatives from four Australian universities, including the University of Melbourne and the University of New South Wales, who had taken part in the Sino-Australian Collegiate Rowing and Dragon Boat Friendship Challenge. Participants gathered with Chinese and international youth based in Canberra to share their vivid experiences of racing on the water in Nanjing and personally immersing themselves in Chinese culture. Ambassador Liu Jingsong engaged warmly and frequently with the attendees during the session. Key points from his remarks are as follows:

Ambassador Liu noted that he had presented his credentials to the Governor-General of Australia just the day before, making today’s exchange with young friends his first public-diplomacy activity since arriving in Australia, which speaks to the important role of youth in the bilateral relationship.

[Canberra Makes Way for Black Swans]

Ambassador Liu said that strolling along the shores of Lake Burley Griffin in central Canberra and looking out over its open, clear waters, his first thought was that this would be a perfect setting for a lively dragon boat race. Upon enquiry, however, he learned that the lake is under strict ecological protection, and that black swans and other wildlife are the “privileged residents” of these waters, making it extremely difficult to stage water sports event here. (Laughter from the room.)
He added that he had travelled to Canberra by plane and coach. The ancient Silk Road, he said, was marked as much by camel bells across desert dunes as by sailing ships dotting the open ocean. Australia, as a vital maritime extension of the Silk Road, enjoys a unique geographical position and abundant tourism resources; there is vast potential ahead for passenger and cargo shipping, especially cruise liners.

[The Origin of the Dragon Boat and the Zongzi and the Oriental Philosophy]

Ambassador Liu noted that many of the Australian students had their very first encounter with dragon boat racing in Nanjing. The sport traces its origins to the commemoration of Qu Yuan, a beloved patriotic poet and statesman from over two millennia ago. According to legend, after Qu Yuan drowned himself in a river in despair over his kingdom’s decline, local people, revering his character, raced out in boats beating drums to drive away fish and shrimp and protect his body. This practice gradually evolved into dragon boat racing. They also cast glutinous rice wrapped in bamboo leaves into the river as an offering; thus the zongzi was born. The dragon boat and the zongzi—one embodying strength, the other tenderness—together carry the cultural core of the Chinese people: Honoring loyalty and righteousness, commemorating the sages of old.

Ambassador Liu observed that Chinese philosophy abounds with water-related wisdom: “Water can carry a boat, but it can also capsize it”, goes one saying. “The benevolent find joy in mountains, the wise find joy in water”, goes another. The mountain's steadfastness and weight, and water's flexibility and fluency, complement each other, forming the spiritual pursuit of the Chinese people. Water, Liu added, can nourish all things, yet it also holds within it the strength to overcome even the toughest challenges.

[Mateship Tested in Storm and Strife]

Ambassador Liu reflected that China and Australia fought a common enemy during the Second World War, which is a living embodiment of the Chinese idiom “tóng zhōu gòng jì” (We are all in the same boat) and the Australian ethos of “mateship”.

During the war, in 1942, when the Lisbon Maru sank, fishermen from Zhoushan, China, braved gunfire in small boats to rescue Allied personnel, including several Australians. In peacetime, in 2023 at Fairy Meadow Beach in Wollongong, New South Wales, Chinese student Jiang Antong sacrificed his life while rescuing an Australian classmate caught in a rip current; the Governor-General of Australia posthumously awarded him a Commendation for Brave Conduct. Recently, when a catastrophic mudslide struck the China-Nepal border area near Gyirong, Xizang, Chinese rescue teams launched immediate search-and-rescue operations, while Australians from all walks of life offered their condolences without delay, showcasing the mutual support between our peoples.

[In striving through adversity, “Growth Matters More Than Results”]

Ambassador Liu congratulated the Australian teams on their outstanding performance at the Nanjing International Universities Rowing Open, noting that the event embodied the spirit of “promoting exchange through competition and forging friendship on the water”. He echoed Chinese tennis player Zheng Qinwen’s sentiment that growth matters more than the scoreline, adding that Medals are certainly dazzling, but victory or defeat is not the essence of competition. The experience of striving together as a team and the friendships forged across the ocean are far more valuable than any trophy.

[Let’s Sway Twin Oars]

Ambassador Liu left the young people with this message: China-Australia friendship requires participation from all sectors and the strength of people of all ages. Each of you is both an envoy for that friendship and a sailor aboard the vessel of China-Australia relations. He encouraged them to “sway the oars together” on the tides of our times, with hearts and minds united in one direction and strength concentrated in one effort, without slacking off, without deviating from course, without retreating, breaking through waves and sailing steadily toward distant horizons.

My fellow black men shaaaa…
Sometimes I dey truly wonder wetin value mean to una for this una tech space for naija.

Somehow somehow, una no see the FREE MENTORSHIP PLATFORM wey we build for Nigerians wey truly wan learn fullstack development but dem no fit afford expensive training.
